sentences.zh: 王播，字明敭。

translations.literal: Wang Bo, Wang Bo, style name Mingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bo, whose style name was Mingyang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖璡，嘉州司馬。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Jin was Vice Governor of Jia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Jin served as vice governor of Jiazhou.

sentences.zh: 祖升，咸陽令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sheng was Magistrate of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sheng was magistrate of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 父恕，揚府參軍。

translations.literal: His father Shu was a staff officer in Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shu served as a staff officer in Yangzhou Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 播擢進士第，登賢良方正制科，授集賢校理，再遷監察御史，轉殿中，歷侍御史。

translations.literal: Bo was selected in the jinshi examination, passed the Exalted and Virtuous Through Straightforward Remonstrance examination, was appointed Collator in the Hall of Assembled Talents, was promoted again to Censor, transferred to the Palace Administration, and served successively as Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Bo passed the jinshi examination and the Exalted and Virtuous Through Straightforward Remonstrance examination, was appointed collator in the Hall of Assembled Talents, was then promoted to censor, transferred to the Palace Administration, and served in turn as attending censor.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，幸臣李實為京兆尹，恃恩頗橫，嘗遇播於途，不避。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenyuan era, the favored minister Li Shi was Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao; relying on favor he was quite overbearing, and once encountered Bo on the road and did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Zhenyuan reign, the favored minister Li Shi was metropolitan governor of Jingzhao. Relying on imperial favor he acted quite arrogantly; once he met Bo on the road and did not yield.

sentences.zh: 故事，尹避臺官。

translations.literal: By precedent, the metropolitan governor yielded to censorial officials.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the metropolitan governor was to yield to censorial officials.

sentences.zh: 播移文詆之；

translations.literal: Bo sent a formal dispatch rebuking him;
translations.idiomatic: Bo sent a formal dispatch rebuking him;

sentences.zh: 實怒，後奏播為三原令，欲挫之。

translations.literal: Shi was angry and later memorialized that Bo be made Magistrate of Sanyuan, intending to humble him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi grew angry and later memorialized to appoint Bo magistrate of Sanyuan, intending to humble him.

sentences.zh: 播受命，趨府謁謝，盡府縣之儀。

translations.literal: Bo accepted the appointment, hurried to the prefectural office to pay respects, and performed all the rites between prefecture and county.
translations.idiomatic: Bo accepted the appointment, hurried to the prefectural office to pay his respects, and performed every rite owed between prefecture and county.

sentences.zh: 及臨所部，政理修明，恃勢豪門，未嘗貸法。

translations.literal: When he took up his jurisdiction, governance was well ordered, and he never granted the law leniency to powerful clans who relied on influence.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took up his jurisdiction, his administration was well ordered, and he never showed leniency in the law to powerful clans.

sentences.zh: 歲終考課，為畿邑之最。

translations.literal: At the year's end in the performance review, he ranked first among the counties of the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: In the year-end performance review he ranked first among the counties of the capital region.

sentences.zh: 實以其人有政術，甚禮重之，頻薦之於上。

translations.literal: Shi considered this man skilled in administration and greatly honored him, frequently recommending him to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Shi considered him skilled in administration, treated him with great respect, and frequently recommended him to the throne.

sentences.zh: 德宗奇之，將不次拔用，會母喪。

translations.literal: Dezong was struck by him and was about to promote him out of turn when his mother died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong was impressed and was about to promote him out of turn when Bo's mother died.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，除駕部郎中，改長安令。

translations.literal: When Shunzong ascended the throne, Bo was appointed Director in the Ministry of the Imperial Stud, then changed to Magistrate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong ascended the throne, Bo was appointed director in the Ministry of the Imperial Stud, then reassigned as magistrate of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 歲中，遷工部郎中，知臺雜，刺舉綱憲，為人所稱。

translations.literal: Within the year he was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Works, managed censorial miscellaneous affairs, prosecuted according to statute, and was praised by others.
translations.idiomatic: Within the year he was promoted to director in the Ministry of Works, took charge of censorial miscellaneous affairs, prosecuted according to statute, and won praise.

sentences.zh: 轉考功郎中，出為虢州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel, then went out as Governor of Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director in the Ministry of Personnel, then went out as governor of Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李巽領鹽鐵，奏為副使、兵部郎中。

translations.literal: Li Xun oversaw salt and iron and memorialized that Bo serve as Vice Commissioner and Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun oversaw salt and iron affairs and memorialized that Bo serve as vice commissioner and director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 元和五年，代李夷簡為御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanhe he replaced Li Yijian as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yuanhe he replaced Li Yijian as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 振舉朝章，百職修舉。

translations.literal: He revived court regulations and all offices were put in order.
translations.idiomatic: He revived court regulations, and every office was brought into order.

sentences.zh: 十月，代許孟容為京兆尹。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he replaced Xu Mengrong as Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he replaced Xu Mengrong as metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 時禁軍諸鎮布列畿內，軍人出入，屬鞬佩劍，往往盜發，難以擒奸。

translations.literal: At the time the forbidden armies and various garrisons were stationed throughout the capital region; when soldiers went in and out wearing sword belts at their waists, theft often broke out and criminals were hard to seize.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the forbidden armies and various garrisons were posted throughout the capital region. Soldiers going in and out wore swords at their belts, theft was frequent, and criminals were hard to catch.

sentences.zh: 布播奏請畿內軍鎮將卒，出入不得持戎具，諸王駙馬權豪之家，不得於畿內按試鷹犬畋獵之具。

translations.literal: Bo memorialized requesting that officers and soldiers of army garrisons within the capital region might not carry weapons when going in and out, and that princes, imperial sons-in-law, and powerful noble households might not test falconry dogs or hunting gear within the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Bo memorialized that troops of garrisons within the capital region must not carry weapons when entering or leaving, and that princes, imperial sons-in-law, and powerful households must not trial falcons, dogs, or hunting gear within the capital region.

sentences.zh: 詔從之，自是奸盜弭息。

translations.literal: The edict approved it, and from then on wickedness and theft subsided.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved this, and from then on thieves and lawbreakers subsided.

sentences.zh: 六年三月，轉刑部侍郎，充諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Punishments and made Commissioner for Salt and Iron Transport on the Various Circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixth year he was transferred to vice minister of punishments and appointed commissioner for salt and iron transport on the various circuits.

sentences.zh: 播長於吏術，雖案牘鞅掌，剖析如流，黠吏詆欺，無不彰敗。

translations.literal: Bo excelled in administrative technique; though documents piled up layer upon layer, he analyzed them like flowing water, and shrewd clerks who deceived—none escaped exposure.
translations.idiomatic: Bo excelled at administration. Though documents piled up in layers, he analyzed them as if they flowed past him, and no shrewd clerk who deceived escaped exposure.

sentences.zh: 時天下多故，法寺議讞，科條繁雜。

translations.literal: At the time there were many troubles in the realm, and when the Bureau of Justice deliberated cases, the statutes were numerous and tangled.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was troubled, and when the Bureau of Justice deliberated cases the statutes were numerous and tangled.

sentences.zh: 播備舉前後格條，置之座右。

translations.literal: Bo collected all regulations before and after and placed them at his right hand.
translations.idiomatic: Bo collected all regulations old and new and kept them at his right hand.

sentences.zh: 凡有詳決，疾速如神。

translations.literal: Whenever there was a detailed judgment, he was swift as a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a detailed judgment was needed, he was swift and uncanny.

sentences.zh: 當時屬僚，嘆服不暇。

translations.literal: His colleagues at the time gasped in admiration without cease.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues at the time marveled without end.

sentences.zh: 十年四月，改禮部尚書，領使如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the tenth year he was changed to Minister of Rites while retaining his commission as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the tenth year he was made minister of rites while retaining his commission as before.

sentences.zh: 先是，李巽以程异為江淮院官，异又通泉貨，及播領使，奏之為副。

translations.literal: Previously Li Xun had Cheng Yi as an official of the Jianghuai salt monopoly; Yi also trafficked in currency, and when Bo took charge of the commission he memorialized to make him Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Xun had appointed Cheng Yi an official of the Jianghuai salt monopoly, and Yi also dealt in currency. When Bo took charge of the commission he memorialized to make Yi his deputy.

sentences.zh: 當王師討吳元濟，令异乘傳往江淮，賦輿大集，以至賊平，深有力焉。

translations.literal: When the imperial army campaigned against Wu Yuanji, he ordered Yi to travel by rapid relay to Jianghuai and immense levies of carriage and transport were assembled; up to the pacification of the rebel he contributed great strength.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army campaigned against Wu Yuanji, he sent Yi by rapid relay to Jianghuai, and vast levies of transport were assembled. Up to the rebel's defeat he contributed great force.

sentences.zh: 及皇甫鎛用事，恐播大用，乃請以使務命程异領之，播守本官而已。

translations.literal: When Huangfu Bo came to power, fearing that Bo would be heavily used, he requested that the commission's duties be assigned to Cheng Yi to manage, while Bo kept only his original office.
translations.idiomatic: When Huangfu Bo came to power, fearing that Bo would be heavily promoted, he had the commission's duties assigned to Cheng Yi while Bo kept only his original office.

sentences.zh: 十三年，檢校戶部尚書、成都尹、劍南西川節度使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was made concurrently Minister of Revenue, Governor of Chengdu, and Military Commissioner of Jiannan West.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was made concurrently minister of revenue, governor of Chengdu, and military commissioner of Jiannan West.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，皇甫鎛貶，播累表求還京師。

translations.literal: When Muzong ascended the throne, Huangfu Bo was demoted and Bo repeatedly memorialized asking to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong ascended the throne, Huangfu Bo was demoted, and Bo repeatedly memorialized asking to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年七月，征還，拜刑部尚書，復領鹽鐵轉運等使。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Changqing he was recalled and appointed Minister of Punishments, again heading the salt and iron transport commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Changqing he was recalled, appointed minister of punishments, and again put in charge of the salt and iron transport commission.

sentences.zh: 十月，兼中書侍郎、平章事，領使如故。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was concurrently Vice Director of the Secretariat and Chief Minister, retaining his commission as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was made concurrently vice director of the Secretariat and chief minister, retaining his commission as before.

sentences.zh: 長慶中，內外權臣，率多假借。

translations.literal: During Changqing, powerful ministers inside and outside mostly borrowed authority improperly.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changqing era, powerful ministers inside and outside the court mostly abused borrowed authority.

sentences.zh: 播因銅鹽擢居輔弼，專以承迎為事，而安危啟沃，不措一言。

translations.literal: Bo, having risen to the chief counselors on the strength of copper and salt profits, devoted himself wholly to currying favor, yet on matters of security and danger offered not a single word of counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Bo had risen to chief counselor on the strength of copper and salt profits and devoted himself wholly to currying favor, yet on matters of security and danger he offered not a single word of counsel.

sentences.zh: 時河北復叛，朝廷用兵。

translations.literal: At the time Hebei rose in rebellion again and the court deployed troops.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei rebelled again, and the court mobilized troops.

sentences.zh: 會裴度自太原入覲，朝野物論，言度不宜居外。

translations.literal: When Pei Du entered court from Taiyuan, public opinion inside and outside said Du should not remain outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Du came to court from Taiyuan, public opinion inside and outside held that he should not remain outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，留度復知政事，以播代度為淮南節度使、檢校右僕射，領使如故。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year Du was kept on to return to administration, and Bo replaced Du as Military Commissioner of Huainan and concurrently Vice Minister of the Right, retaining his commission as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the following year Du was kept at court to resume administration, and Bo replaced him as military commissioner of Huainan and concurrently vice director of the right, retaining his commission as before.

sentences.zh: 仍請攜鹽鐵印赴鎮，上都院印，請別給賜，從之。

translations.literal: He also requested to take the salt and iron seal to his post; the seal of the capital monopoly office was to be separately bestowed—this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to take the salt and iron seal to his post while a separate seal for the capital monopoly office was to be bestowed—this was granted.

sentences.zh: 播至淮南，屬歲旱儉，人相啖食，課最不充，設法掊斂，比屋嗟怨。

translations.literal: When Bo reached Huainan, the year was drought-stricken and lean; people ate one another; tax quotas could not be met; he devised methods of extortion and every household groaned in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When Bo reached Huainan, drought and famine struck; people ate one another; tax quotas could not be met; he devised methods of extortion, and every household groaned in resentment.

sentences.zh: 敬宗即位，就加銀青光祿大夫、檢校司空，罷鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: When Jingzong ascended the throne, Bo was promoted on the spot to Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Golden Pocket and concurrently Minister of Works, and was removed from the salt and iron transport commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jingzong ascended the throne, Bo was promoted on the spot to grand master of splendid brightness with golden pocket and concurrently minister of works, and was removed from the salt and iron transport commission.

sentences.zh: 時中尉王守澄用事，播自落利權，廣求珍異，令腹心吏內結守澄，以為之助。

translations.literal: At the time the chief eunuch Wang Shoucheng held power; Bo, having lost his profitable post, widely sought rare objects and had trusted clerks secretly win over Shoucheng to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: The chief eunuch Wang Shoucheng held power. Having lost his profitable post, Bo widely sought rare objects and had trusted clerks secretly win over Shoucheng to aid him.

sentences.zh: 守澄乘閑啟奏，言播有才，上於延英言之。

translations.literal: Shoucheng seized an opportunity to memorialize the throne that Bo had talent; the emperor spoke of it at Yanying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Shoucheng seized an opportunity to memorialize that Bo had talent; the emperor spoke of it at Yanying Hall.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫獨孤朗、張仲方，起居郎孔敏行、柳公權、宋申錫，補闕韋仁實、劉敦儒，拾遺李景讓、薛廷老等，請開延英面奏播之奸邪，交結寵幸，復求大用。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials Dugu Lang and Zhang Zhongfang, Masters of Rectitude Kong Minxing, Liu Gongquan, and Song Shenshen, Repletion Officials Wei Renshi and Liu Dunru, and Reminder Officials Li Jingrang and Xue Tinglao and others requested to open Yanying for a face-to-face memorial on Bo's wickedness, his collusion with favored minions, and his seeking great office again.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials Dugu Lang and Zhang Zhongfang, masters of rectitude Kong Minxing, Liu Gongquan, and Song Shenshen, repletion officials Wei Renshi and Liu Dunru, and reminder officials Li Jingrang and Xue Tinglao and others asked to open Yanying Hall for a face-to-face memorial on Bo's wickedness, his collusion with favored minions, and his seeking high office again.

sentences.zh: 天子沖幼，不能用其言。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was young and could not employ their counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was young and could not act on their counsel.

sentences.zh: 自是，物議紛然不息。

translations.literal: From then on public talk seethed without end.
translations.idiomatic: From then on public talk seethed without end.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，播復領鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year Bo again took charge of the salt and iron transport commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year Bo again took charge of the salt and iron transport commission.

sentences.zh: 播既得舊職，乃於銅鹽之內，巧為賦斂，以事月進。

translations.literal: Once he regained his former post, he artfully levied within copper and salt profits, presenting monthly tributes.
translations.idiomatic: Once he regained his former post, he artfully levied within copper and salt profits and presented monthly tributes to the throne.

sentences.zh: 名為羨余，其實正額，務希獎擢，不恤人言。

translations.literal: He called them surplus revenue but they were in fact regular quotas; he sought favor and promotion and cared nothing for what people said.
translations.idiomatic: He called them surplus revenue, but they were in fact regular quotas; he sought favor and promotion and cared nothing for public opinion.

sentences.zh: 時揚州城內官河水淺，遇旱即滯漕船。

translations.literal: At the time the official river within Yangzhou city was shallow, and in drought grain-transport ships were blocked.
translations.idiomatic: The official river within Yangzhou city was shallow, and in drought grain-transport ships were stranded.

sentences.zh: 乃奏自城南閶門西七里港開河向東，屈曲取禪智寺橋通舊官河，開鑿稍深，舟航易濟；

translations.literal: He memorialized to open a canal eastward from Qili Harbor seven li west of the Chang Gate in the south of the city, winding to connect with the old official river via the Chanzhisi Bridge; the excavation was somewhat deep and shipping was eased;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to open a canal eastward from Qili Harbor, seven li west of the Chang Gate in the south of the city, winding to connect with the old official river via the Chanzhisi Bridge; the excavation was made somewhat deeper and shipping was eased;

sentences.zh: 所開長一十九里，其工役料度，不破省錢，當使方圓自備，而漕運不阻。

translations.literal: The length opened was nineteen li; labor and materials were to be supplied by the local circuit without drawing on provincial funds, and grain transport would not be obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: The canal opened was nineteen li long; labor and materials were to be supplied by the local circuit without drawing on provincial funds, and grain transport would not be obstructed.

sentences.zh: 後政賴之。

translations.literal: Later administrations relied on it.
translations.idiomatic: Later administrations relied on it.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，就加檢校司徒。

translations.literal: When Wenzong ascended the throne, Bo was promoted on the spot to concurrently Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, Bo was promoted on the spot to concurrently grand mentor.

sentences.zh: 太和元年五月，自淮南入覲，進大小銀碗三千四百枚、綾絹二十萬匹。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Taihe he entered court from Huainan, presenting three thousand four hundred large and small silver bowls and two hundred thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Taihe he came to court from Huainan, presenting three thousand four hundred large and small silver bowls and two hundred thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 六月，拜尚書左僕射、同平章事，領使如故。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he was appointed Vice Director of the Left of the Ministry and Chief Minister, retaining his commission as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was appointed vice director of the left ministry and chief minister, retaining his commission as before.

sentences.zh: 二年，進封太原公、太清宮使。

translations.literal: In the second year he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Taiyuan and made Commissioner of the Taqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Taiyuan and made commissioner of the Taqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，患喉腫暴卒，時年七十二。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year he died suddenly of a swollen throat at age seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year he died suddenly of a swollen throat at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 廢朝三日，贈太尉。

translations.literal: Court mourning was suspended for three days and he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Court was suspended for three days of mourning, and he was posthumously enfeoffed as grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 播出自單門，以文辭自立；

translations.literal: Bo came from a humble lineage and established himself through literary skill;
translations.idiomatic: Bo came from a humble lineage and established himself through literary skill;

sentences.zh: 踐升華顯，郁有能名。

translations.literal: he climbed to splendor and bore a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: he rose to splendor and bore a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 而隨勢沈浮，不存士行；

translations.literal: Yet he drifted with circumstances and did not preserve the conduct of a gentleman;
translations.idiomatic: Yet he drifted with circumstances and did not preserve the conduct of a gentleman;

sentences.zh: 奸邪進取，君子恥之。

translations.literal: winning advancement through wickedness—men of character were ashamed of him.
translations.idiomatic: winning advancement through wickedness—men of character were ashamed of him.

sentences.zh: 然天性勤於吏事，使務填委，胥吏盈廷取決，簿書堆案盈幾，他人若不堪勝，而播用此為適。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was diligent in administrative affairs; when commission business piled up, clerks filled the court awaiting decisions and documents heaped on the desk to overflow the tables—if others could not endure it, Bo took this as his element.
translations.idiomatic: Yet by nature he was diligent in administrative affairs. When commission business piled up, clerks filled the court awaiting decisions and documents heaped on the desk until the tables overflowed—what others could not endure, Bo took as his element.

sentences.zh: 播子式，弟炎、起。

translations.literal: Bo's son Shi, and younger brothers Yan and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Bo's son was Shi; his younger brothers were Yan and Qi.

sentences.zh: 炎，貞元十五年登進士第，累官至太常博士，早世。

translations.literal: Yan passed the jinshi in the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan, rose in office to Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and died young.
translations.idiomatic: Yan passed the jinshi in the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan, rose in office to doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and died young.

sentences.zh: 子鐸、鐐。

translations.literal: His sons Duo and Liao.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Duo and Liao.

sentences.zh: 起，字舉之，貞元十四年擢進士第，釋褐集賢校理，登制策直言極諫科，授藍田尉。

translations.literal: Qi, style name Juzhi, passed the jinshi in the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan, left office as Collator in the Hall of Assembled Talents, entered the Straightforward Remonstrance examination, and was appointed Magistrate of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, whose style name was Juzhi, passed the jinshi in the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan, took his first post as collator in the Hall of Assembled Talents, passed the Straightforward Remonstrance examination, and was appointed magistrate of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 宰相李吉甫鎮淮南，以監察充掌書記。

translations.literal: When Chief Minister Li Jifu governed Huainan, he served as recording secretary while acting as censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Chief Minister Li Jifu governed Huainan, Qi served as his recording secretary while acting as censor.

sentences.zh: 入朝為殿中，遷起居郎、司勛員外郎、直史館。

translations.literal: On entering court he served in the Palace Administration, was promoted to Master of Rectitude, Junior Director in the Ministry of Merits, and duty Editor of the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: On entering court he served in the Palace Administration, was promoted to master of rectitude, junior director in the Ministry of Merits, and duty editor of the History Office.

sentences.zh: 元和十四年，以比部郎中知制誥。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Yuanhe he was Junior Director in the Ministry of Revenue in charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Yuanhe he was junior director in the Ministry of Revenue in charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Muzong ascended the throne he was appointed Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong ascended the throne he was appointed drafting attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年，遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changqing he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Changqing he was promoted to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 其年，錢徽掌貢士，為朝臣請托，人以為濫。

translations.literal: That year Qian Hui oversaw the civil examinations; court officials made requests on behalf of candidates and people considered it improper.
translations.idiomatic: That year Qian Hui oversaw the civil examinations; court officials made requests on behalf of candidates, and people considered the process corrupt.

sentences.zh: 詔起與同職白居易覆試，覆落者多。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Qi, together with his colleague Bai Juyi, to conduct a reexamination; many who had passed were failed on review.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Qi, together with his colleague Bai Juyi, to conduct a reexamination; many who had passed were failed on review.

sentences.zh: 徽貶官，起遂代徽為禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Hui was demoted and Qi then replaced Hui as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was demoted, and Qi then replaced him as vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 掌貢二年，得士尤精。

translations.literal: For two years in charge of the examinations he selected candidates of exceptional quality.
translations.idiomatic: For two years in charge of the examinations he selected candidates of exceptional quality.

sentences.zh: 先是，貢舉猥濫，勢門子弟，交相酬酢；

translations.literal: Previously the examinations had been corrupt and excessive, and sons of powerful houses exchanged favors;
translations.idiomatic: Previously the examinations had been corrupt and excessive, and sons of powerful houses exchanged favors;

sentences.zh: 寒門俊造，十棄六七。

translations.literal: talented men from poor families were rejected seven or eight out of ten.
translations.idiomatic: talented men from poor families were rejected seven or eight out of ten.

sentences.zh: 及元稹、李紳在翰林，深怒其事，故有覆試之科。

translations.literal: When Yuan Zhen and Li Shen were in the Hanlin Academy they deeply hated this matter, hence the institution of the reexamination.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Zhen and Li Shen were in the Hanlin Academy they deeply resented this, hence the institution of the reexamination.

sentences.zh: 及起考貢士，奏當司所選進士，據所考雜文，先送中書，令宰臣閱視可否，然後下當司放榜。

translations.literal: When Qi conducted the examinations he memorialized that jinshi candidates selected by his office, according to the miscellaneous compositions examined, should first be sent to the Secretariat for the chief ministers to review whether they were acceptable, and only then would his office post the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi conducted the examinations he memorialized that jinshi candidates selected by his office, on the basis of the compositions examined, should first be sent to the Secretariat for the chief ministers to review, and only then would his office post the rolls.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: This was approved.

sentences.zh: 議者以為起雖避是非，失貢職也，故出為河南尹。

translations.literal: Critics held that though Qi avoided controversy, he had failed the duty of the examinations, and so he was sent out as Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Critics held that though Qi avoided controversy, he had failed the duty of the examinations, and so he was sent out as governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 入為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He entered court as Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，加集賢學士、判院事。

translations.literal: When Wenzong ascended the throne he was added as Academician of the Hall of Assembled Talents and Acting Director of the Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne he was added as academician of the Hall of Assembled Talents and acting director of the academy.

sentences.zh: 以兄播為僕射輔政，不欲典選部，改兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Because his elder brother Bo was Vice Director of the Left assisting in government, he did not wish to oversee the selection office and was changed to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Because his elder brother Bo was vice director of the left assisting in government, he did not wish to oversee the selection office and was reassigned as vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 太和二年，出為陜虢觀察使、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe he went out as Military Governor of Shaan-Guo Circuit and concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taihe he went out as military governor of Shaan-Guo Circuit and concurrently censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 四年，入拜尚書左丞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he entered court as appointed Vice Director of the Left Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he entered court as vice director of the left ministry.

sentences.zh: 居播之喪，號毀過禮，友悌尤至。

translations.literal: While in mourning for Bo he wailed beyond what ritual prescribed, and fraternal affection was especially deep.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning Bo he wailed beyond what ritual prescribed, and his fraternal affection was especially deep.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部尚書、判度支。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Revenue in charge of the Bureau of Budgets.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of revenue in charge of the Bureau of Budgets.

sentences.zh: 以西北邊備，歲有和市以給軍，勞人饋挽，奏於靈武，邠寧起營田。

translations.literal: Because the northwestern frontier required annual market purchases to supply the army, burdening the people with transport, he memorialized to establish army farms at Lingwu and in the Bian-Ning line.
translations.idiomatic: Because the northwestern frontier required annual market purchases to supply the army, burdening the people with transport, he memorialized to establish army farms at Lingwu and along the Bian-Ning line.

sentences.zh: 六年，檢校吏部尚書、河中尹、河中晉絳節度使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was made concurrently Minister of Personnel, Governor of Hezhong, and Military Commissioner of Hezhong-Jin-Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made concurrently minister of personnel, governor of Hezhong, and military commissioner of Hezhong-Jin-Jiang.

sentences.zh: 時屬蝗旱，粟價暴踴，豪門閉糴，以邀善價。

translations.literal: Locusts and drought struck that year; grain prices soared; powerful households hoarded grain to force a good price.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts and drought struck that year; grain prices soared; powerful households hoarded grain to force favorable prices.

sentences.zh: 起嚴誡儲蓄之家，出粟於市，隱者致之於法，由是民獲濟焉。

translations.literal: Qi sternly warned granary households to release grain to market; those who concealed grain were brought to justice, and thereby the people were relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Qi sternly warned granary households to release grain to market; those who concealed grain were brought to justice, and thereby the people were relieved.

sentences.zh: 七年，入為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he entered court as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he entered court as minister of war.

sentences.zh: 八年，檢校右僕射、襄州刺史，充山南東道節度。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was made concurrently Vice Director of the Right, Governor of Xiang Prefecture, and Military Commissioner of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was made concurrently vice director of the right, governor of Xiang Prefecture, and military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 江、漢水田，前政撓法，塘堰缺壞。

translations.literal: The rice fields of the Yangzi and Han rivers—previous administrators had bent the law, and ponds and dikes were broken and ruined.
translations.idiomatic: In the rice fields along the Yangzi and Han rivers, previous administrators had bent the law, and ponds and dikes lay broken and ruined.

sentences.zh: 起下車，命從事李業行屬郡，檢視而補繕，特為水法，民無兇年。

translations.literal: When Qi took up his post, he ordered his staff member Li Ye to visit the subordinate prefectures, inspect and repair them, established special water regulations, and the people had no years of famine.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took up his post, he sent his staff officer Li Ye through the subordinate prefectures to inspect and repair the works, established special water regulations, and the people suffered no famine years.

sentences.zh: 九年，就加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was further promoted to Grand Master with Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was further promoted to grand master with silver seal and blue ribbon.

sentences.zh: 時李訓用事，訓即起貢舉門生也，欲援起為相。

translations.literal: At that time Li Xun held power; Xun was Qi's examination pupil and wished to promote Qi to chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Xun held power; Xun had been Qi's pupil from the civil examinations and wished to promote Qi to chief minister.

sentences.zh: 八月，詔拜兵部侍郎，判戶部事。

translations.literal: In the eighth month an edict appointed him Vice Minister of War in charge of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month an edict appointed him vice minister of war in charge of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 其冬，訓敗，起以儒素長者，人不以為累，但罷判戶部事。

translations.literal: That winter Xun was defeated; as Qi was regarded as a plain Confucian elder, people did not consider him implicated, but he was only removed from charge of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Xun fell from power; because Qi was regarded as a plain, upright Confucian elder, people did not consider him implicated, and he was only removed from charge of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 文宗好文，尤尚古學。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong loved literature and especially valued ancient learning.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong loved literature and especially prized ancient learning.

sentences.zh: 鄭覃長於經義，起長於博洽，俱引翰林，講論經史。

translations.literal: Zheng Tan excelled in canonical meaning, Qi excelled in broad erudition; both were brought into the Hanlin Academy to lecture on the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan excelled in the meaning of the classics, while Qi excelled in broad erudition; both were brought into the Hanlin Academy to lecture on the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 起僻於嗜學，雖官位崇重，耽玩無篸；

translations.literal: Qi was singularly devoted to the love of learning; though his official rank was lofty and weighty, he indulged in study without satiety;
translations.idiomatic: Qi was singularly devoted to learning; though his official rank was lofty, he indulged in study without ever growing weary of it;

sentences.zh: 夙夜孜孜，殆忘寢食，書無不覽，經目靡遺。

translations.literal: Day and night he was diligent and tireless, almost forgetting sleep and food; there was no book he did not read, and nothing that passed before his eyes was left out.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night he worked tirelessly, almost forgetting sleep and food; he read every book he could find and forgot nothing that passed before his eyes.

sentences.zh: 轉兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of war.

sentences.zh: 以莊恪太子登儲，欲令儒者授經，乃兼太子侍讀，判太常卿，充禮儀詳定使，創造禮神九玉，奏議曰：

translations.literal: Because the Prince of Zhuangke was established as heir, wishing to have Confucian scholars teach the classics, he was additionally made Preceptor to the Heir Apparent, Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Commissioner for Detailed Determination of Ritual; he created the nine jades for honoring the spirits and submitted a memorial stating:
translations.idiomatic: Because the Prince of Zhuangke had been established as heir and the court wished to have Confucian scholars teach him the classics, Qi was additionally made preceptor to the heir apparent, acting director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and commissioner for detailed determination of ritual; he designed the nine jades for honoring the spirits and submitted a memorial stating:

sentences.zh: 邦國之禮，祀為大事；

translations.literal: In the rites of state, sacrifice is a great affair;
translations.idiomatic: In the rites of a state, sacrifice is a matter of the greatest importance;

sentences.zh: 珪璧之議，經有前規。

translations.literal: The discussion of jade tablets and disks has prior regulations in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: The discussion of jade tablets and disks already has established precedents in the classics.

sentences.zh: 謹按《周禮》：「天地四方，以蒼璧禮天，黃琮禮地，青珪禮東方，赤璋禮南方，白琥禮西方，黑璜禮北方。」

translations.literal: Respectfully according to the Rites of Zhou: "Heaven and earth and the four directions—with the azure bi honor heaven, with the yellow cong honor earth, with the green gui honor the east, with the red zhang honor the south, with the white hu honor the west, and with the black huang honor the north.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully according to the Rites of Zhou: "For heaven and earth and the four directions, the azure bi honors heaven, the yellow cong honors earth, the green gui honors the east, the red zhang honors the south, the white hu honors the west, and the black huang honors the north.

sentences.zh: 又云：「四圭有邸以祀天」，「兩圭有邸以祀地」，「圭璧以祀日月星辰」。

translations.literal: It also says: "Four gui with bases to sacrifice to heaven," "Two gui with bases to sacrifice to earth," "Gui and bi to sacrifice to the sun, moon, stars, and constellations."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "Four gui with bases are used to sacrifice to heaven," "Two gui with bases are used to sacrifice to earth," and "Gui and bi are used to sacrifice to the sun, moon, stars, and constellations."

sentences.zh: 凡此九器，皆祀神之玉也。

translations.literal: All these nine vessels are jades for sacrificing to the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: All nine of these vessels are jades used in sacrificing to the spirits.

sentences.zh: 又云：「以禋祀祀昊天上帝。」

translations.literal: It also says: "With the yin sacrifice sacrifice to the Supreme God of the Vast Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "With the yin sacrifice one sacrifices to the Supreme God of the Vast Heaven.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云：「禋，煙也，為玉幣，祭訖燔之，而升煙以報陽也。」

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan says: "Yin means smoke; jade silks are made, and after the sacrifice ends they are burned, sending up smoke to report to the yang."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan says: "Yin means smoke; jade silks are prepared, and after the sacrifice is finished they are burned, sending up smoke to report to the yang principle."

sentences.zh: 今與《開元禮》義同，此則焚玉之驗也。

translations.literal: Now this agrees with the meaning of the Kaiyuan Rites; this is proof of burning jade.
translations.idiomatic: This now agrees with the meaning of the Kaiyuan Rites, and is proof that jade was burned.

sentences.zh: 又《周禮》：「掌國之玉鎮大寶器，若大祭，既事而藏之。」

translations.literal: Also in the Rites of Zhou: "In charge of the state's jade treasure-weights and great precious vessels—when a great sacrifice is finished, they are stored away.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou also states: "In charge of the state's jade treasure-weights and great precious vessels—when a great sacrifice is finished, they are stored away.

sentences.zh: 此則收玉之證也。

translations.literal: This is proof of collecting and storing jade.
translations.idiomatic: This is proof that jade was collected and stored after the rite.

sentences.zh: 梁代崔靈恩撰《三禮義宗》云：「凡祭天神，各有二玉：一以禮神，一則燔之。

translations.literal: Cui Ling'en of the Liang dynasty wrote in the Comprehensive Meaning of the Three Rites: "For every sacrifice to heavenly spirits, there are two jades: one to honor the spirit, and one to be burned.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ling'en of the Liang dynasty wrote in the Comprehensive Meaning of the Three Rites: "For every sacrifice to heavenly spirits, there are two jades: one to honor the spirit, and one to be burned.

sentences.zh: 禮神者，訖事卻收；

translations.literal: The one for honoring the spirit is collected back when the service is finished;
translations.idiomatic: The jade used to honor the spirit is collected back when the rite is finished;

sentences.zh: 祀神者，與牲俱燎。」

translations.literal: The one for sacrificing to the spirit is burned together with the sacrificial animals.
translations.idiomatic: The jade used in sacrificing to the spirit is burned together with the sacrificial animals.

sentences.zh: 則靈恩之義，合於《禮經》。

translations.literal: Then Ling'en's meaning accords with the Ritual Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Ling'en's interpretation thus accords with the Ritual Classics.

sentences.zh: 今國家郊天祀地，祀神之玉常用；

translations.literal: Now when the state sacrifices to heaven at the suburbs and sacrifices to earth, the jades for sacrificing to the spirits are regularly used;
translations.idiomatic: Today, when the state sacrifices to heaven at the suburbs and to earth, the jades used in sacrificing to the spirits are regularly employed;

sentences.zh: 守經據古，禮神之玉則無。

translations.literal: But following the classics and relying on antiquity, there are no jades for honoring the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if one follows the classics and relies on antiquity, there are no jades for honoring the spirits.

sentences.zh: 臣等請下有司，精求良玉，創造蒼璧、黃琮等九器，祭訖則藏之。

translations.literal: We your ministers request that orders be sent to the relevant offices to carefully seek fine jade and create the nine vessels including the azure bi and yellow cong; when the sacrifice is finished they shall be stored away.
translations.idiomatic: We your ministers request that orders be sent to the relevant offices to carefully seek fine jade and create the nine vessels, including the azure bi and yellow cong, to be stored away after each sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 其燎玉即依常制。

translations.literal: The jades for burning shall follow the usual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The jades to be burned should follow the usual regulations.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 為太子廣《五運圖》及《文場秀句》等獻之。

translations.literal: He compiled and expanded the Five Circuits Diagram and Elegant Lines from the Literary Arena, etc., and presented them to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled and expanded the Five Circuits Diagram and Elegant Lines from the Literary Arena, among other works, and presented them to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 三年，以本官充翰林侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the third year, with his existing office he was made Hanlin Lecturing Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, while retaining his existing office, he was made Hanlin lecturing academician.

sentences.zh: 莊恪太子薨，詔起為哀冊文，辭情婉麗。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Zhuangke died, an edict ordered Qi to compose the mourning eulogy; its language was tender and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Zhuangke died, an edict ordered Qi to compose the mourning eulogy; its language was tender and beautiful.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷太子少師，判兵部事，侍講如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to Junior Preceptor to the Heir Apparent, in charge of the Ministry of War, with lecturing duties unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to junior preceptor to the heir apparent, placed in charge of the Ministry of War, and continued his lecturing duties as before.

sentences.zh: 以其家貧，特詔每月割仙韶院月料錢三百千添給。

translations.literal: Because his household was poor, a special edict ordered that each month three hundred thousand cash from the Xianshao Academy's monthly stipend be additionally allocated to him.
translations.idiomatic: Because his household was poor, a special edict ordered that each month an additional three hundred thousand cash be taken from the Xianshao Academy's monthly stipend and given to him.

sentences.zh: 起富於文學，而理家無法，俸料入門，即為仆妾所有。

translations.literal: Qi was rich in literary learning but had no method in managing the household; once salary entered the door it became the property of servants and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was rich in literary learning but had no method in managing his household; as soon as his salary entered the door it became the property of his servants and concubines.

sentences.zh: 帝以師友之恩，特加周給。

translations.literal: The emperor, out of the kindness owed to a teacher and friend, specially added further provision.
translations.idiomatic: Out of the kindness owed to a teacher and friend, the emperor specially added further provision.

sentences.zh: 議者以與伶官分給，可為恥之。

translations.literal: Commentators considered sharing allocation with entertainers something shameful.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators considered it shameful that he was given a share of the same stipend as palace entertainers.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，八月，充山陵鹵簿使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong ascended the throne, in the eighth month he was made Commissioner of the Imperial Procession for the Mountain Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong ascended the throne, in the eighth month Qi was made commissioner of the imperial procession for the mountain tomb.

sentences.zh: 樞密使劉弘逸、薛季稜懼誅，欲因山陵兵士謀廢立。

translations.literal: The Palace Commissioners Liu Hongyi and Xue Jiling feared execution and wished to use the tomb-guard soldiers to plot deposing and enthroning.
translations.idiomatic: The palace commissioners Liu Hongyi and Xue Jiling feared execution and wished to use the tomb-guard soldiers in a plot to depose the emperor and install another.

sentences.zh: 起與山陵使知其謀，密奏，皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Qi and the tomb commissioner learned of their plot, secretly memorialized, and all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Qi and the tomb commissioner learned of the plot, secretly memorialized the throne, and all the conspirators were executed.

sentences.zh: 尋檢校左僕射、東都留守，判東都尚書省事。

translations.literal: Soon he was made concurrently Vice Director of the Left, Defender of the Eastern Capital, in charge of the Eastern Capital Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made concurrently vice director of the left, defender of the Eastern Capital, and placed in charge of the Eastern Capital Ministry of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 會昌元年，征拜吏部尚書，判太常卿事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huichang he was summoned and appointed Minister of Personnel, in charge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huichang he was summoned and appointed minister of personnel, placed in charge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 三年，權知禮部貢舉。

translations.literal: In the third year he was acting overseer of the Ministry of Rites civil examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he served as acting overseer of the Ministry of Rites civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 明年，正拜左僕射，復知貢舉。

translations.literal: The next year he was formally appointed Vice Director of the Left and again oversaw the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was formally appointed vice director of the left and again oversaw the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 起前後四典貢部，所選皆當代辭藝之士，有名於時，人皆賞其精鑒徇公也。

translations.literal: Qi four times in succession oversaw the examination bureau; those he selected were all men of literary talent of the age, famous in their time, and people all praised his keen discernment and public-mindedness.
translations.idiomatic: Qi oversaw the examination bureau on four separate occasions; those he selected were all men of literary talent who were famous in their day, and people praised his keen judgment and public-minded fairness.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，出為興元尹，兼同平章事，充山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: That autumn he went out as Governor of Xingyuan, concurrently Co-ordinating Chief Minister, and Military Commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he went out as governor of Xingyuan, concurrently co-ordinating chief minister, and military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 赴鎮日，延英辭。

translations.literal: On the day he departed for his command, he took leave at Yanching Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he departed for his post, he took leave of the emperor in Yanching Hall.

sentences.zh: 帝謂之曰：「卿國之耆老，宰相無內外，朕有闕政，飛表以聞。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to him: "You are the nation's elder; chief ministers know no inside or outside; if I have failures in government, send a swift memorial to inform me.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to him: "You are the nation's elder statesman; for a chief minister there is no distinction between inside and outside the court—if I fail in government, send me a swift memorial at once.

sentences.zh: 宴賜頗厚。

translations.literal: He was generously feasted and rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave him a generous farewell feast and rewards.

sentences.zh: 在鎮二年，以老疾求代，不許。

translations.literal: After two years at his command, he requested replacement due to old age and illness, but it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: After two years at his post he requested a replacement because of old age and illness, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 大中元年，卒於鎮，時年八十八。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong he died at his command, aged eighty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dazhong he died at his post, at the age of eighty-eight.

sentences.zh: 廢朝三日，贈太尉，謚曰文懿。

translations.literal: Court was suspended for three days; he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, posthumous title Wenyì.
translations.idiomatic: Court was suspended for three days; he was posthumously granted grand preceptor, with the posthumous title Wenyì (Cultured and Virtuous).

sentences.zh: 文集一百二十卷，《五緯圖》十卷，《寫宣》十卷。

translations.literal: Collected works in 120 scrolls, Five Weft Diagram in 10 scrolls, Written Responses in 10 scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to 120 scrolls; he also wrote the Five Weft Diagram in 10 scrolls and Written Responses in 10 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 起侍講時，或僻字疑事，令中使口宣，即以榜子對，故名曰《寫宣》。

translations.literal: When Qi served as lecturer, if obscure characters or doubtful matters arose, the emperor would have palace envoys orally announce them, and Qi would respond with written slips; hence the title Written Responses.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi served as lecturer, if obscure characters or doubtful matters arose, the emperor would have palace envoys announce them orally, and Qi would answer with written slips; hence the title Written Responses.

sentences.zh: 子龜嗣。

translations.literal: His son Gui succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gui succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 龜，字大年。

translations.literal: Gui, style name Danian.
translations.idiomatic: Gui, whose style name was Danian.

sentences.zh: 性簡淡蕭灑，不樂仕進。

translations.literal: His nature was simple, detached, and free and easy; he did not enjoy pursuing office.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was simple, detached, and free-spirited, and he took no pleasure in pursuing office.

sentences.zh: 少以詩酒琴書自適，不從科試。

translations.literal: From youth he satisfied himself with poetry, wine, the zither, and books, and did not take the civil examinations.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he contented himself with poetry, wine, the zither, and books, and never took the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 京城光福裏第，起兄弟同居，斯為宏敞。

translations.literal: The residence in Guangfu Lane in the capital where Qi and his brothers lived together was vast and spacious.
translations.idiomatic: The residence in Guangfu Lane in the capital, where Qi and his brothers lived together, was vast and spacious.

sentences.zh: 龜意在人外，倦接朋遊，乃於永達裏園林深僻處創書齋，吟嘯其間，目為「半隱亭」。

translations.literal: Gui's mind was beyond ordinary men; weary of mingling with friends, he built a study in a deep secluded spot in the garden at Yongda Lane, composing and reciting there, and called it the "Half-Reclusion Pavilion."
translations.idiomatic: Gui's mind was set on matters beyond ordinary life; weary of social gatherings, he built a study in a deep, secluded corner of the garden at Yongda Lane, where he composed and recited poetry, and called it the "Half-Reclusion Pavilion."

sentences.zh: 及從父起在河中，於中條山谷中起草堂，與山人道士遊，朔望一還府第，後人目為「郎君谷」。

translations.literal: When his uncle Qi was in Hezhong, he built a thatched hall in the Zhongtiao mountain valley, associating with mountain recluses and Daoist priests, returning to the mansion once on the first and fifteenth of the month; later people called it "The Young Master's Valley."
translations.idiomatic: When his uncle Qi was in Hezhong, Gui built a thatched hall in the Zhongtiao mountain valley, where he associated with mountain recluses and Daoist priests and returned to the family mansion only on the first and fifteenth of each month; later people called the place "The Young Master's Valley."

sentences.zh: 及起保厘東周，龜於龍門西谷構松齋，棲息往來，放懷事外。

translations.literal: When Qi was charged with preserving and comforting the Eastern Zhou capital, Gui built the Pine Study in the western valley of Longmen, dwelling and coming and going there, releasing his cares in affairs beyond the world.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was charged with preserving and comforting the Eastern Zhou capital, Gui built the Pine Study in the western valley of Longmen, where he lived and traveled back and forth, freeing his mind from worldly cares.

sentences.zh: 起鎮興元，又於漢陽之龍山立隱舍，每浮舟而往，其閑逸如此。

translations.literal: When Qi governed Xingyuan, he again established a reclusion lodge on Dragon Mountain in Hanyang; each time he would go by boat, so leisurely was he.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi governed Xingyuan, Gui again established a reclusion lodge on Dragon Mountain in Hanyang, traveling there each time by boat—so leisurely was his way of life.

sentences.zh: 武宗知之，以左拾遺征。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong learned of him and summoned him as Left Remonstrance Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong learned of him and summoned him to office as left remonstrance clerk.

sentences.zh: 久之，方至殿廷一謝，陳情曰：「臣才疏散，無用於時，加以疾病所嬰，不任祿仕。

translations.literal: After a long time he finally came to the court hall once to give thanks, stating his situation: "Your subject's talents are scattered and loose, useless to the age; moreover I am afflicted by illness and cannot bear salary and office.
translations.idiomatic: After a long delay he finally came to the court hall once to give thanks, stating his situation: "Your subject's talents are scattered and of no use to the age; moreover I am afflicted by illness and am unfit for salary and office.

sentences.zh: 臣父年將九十，作鎮遠籓，喜懼之年，闕於供侍。

translations.literal: My father is nearly ninety, holding command in a distant frontier; in these years of joy and fear I lack him in attending morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: My father is nearly ninety and holds command in a distant frontier; in these years when joy and fear alternate, I am unable to attend him morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 乞罷今職，以奉晨昏。」

translations.literal: I beg to be relieved of my present office to serve him morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: I beg to be relieved of my present office so that I may serve him morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 上優詔許之。

translations.literal: The emperor graciously issued an edict approval.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a gracious edict granting his request.

sentences.zh: 明年，丁父憂。

translations.literal: The next year he entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he entered mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 服闋，以右補闕征，遷侍御史、尚書郎。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was summoned as Right Supplementation Clerk, promoted to Attending Censor and Director in a Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was summoned as right supplementation clerk, then promoted to attending censor and director in a ministry.

sentences.zh: 大中末，出為宣歙團練觀察副使，賜緋。

translations.literal: Late in Dazhong he went out as Deputy Military Training Commissioner and Inspector of Xuan-She, granted crimson robes.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Dazhong reign he went out as deputy military training commissioner and inspector of Xuan-She, and was granted crimson robes.

sentences.zh: 入為祠部郎中、史館修撰。

translations.literal: He entered court as Junior Director in the Ministry of Rites and Compiler of the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as junior director in the Ministry of Rites and compiler of the History Office.

sentences.zh: 前從崔玙貳宣歙，及玙鎮河中，又奏為副使。

translations.literal: Previously he had served under Cui Yu as deputy in Xuan-She; when Yu governed Hezhong, he again memorialized to make him deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Previously he had served under Cui Yu as deputy commissioner in Xuan-She; when Yu governed Hezhong, Yu again memorialized to appoint him deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 入為兵部郎中，賜金紫，尋知制誥。

translations.literal: He entered court as Junior Director in the Ministry of War, was granted gold seal and purple robe, and soon was put in charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as junior director in the Ministry of War, was granted gold seal and purple robe, and soon was put in charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 咸通末，以弟鐸在中書，不欲在禁掖，改太常少卿，尋檢校右散騎常侍、同州刺史。

translations.literal: Late in Xiantong, because his younger brother Duo was in the Secretariat, not wishing to be in the inner palace precincts, he was changed to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and soon was made concurrently Right Palatial Aid and Governor of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Xiantong reign, because his younger brother Duo served in the Secretariat, Gui did not wish to remain in the inner palace precincts; he was reassigned as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and soon was made concurrently right palatial aid and governor of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 牙將白約者，甚狡蠹，前後防禦使不能制。

translations.literal: A military officer named Bai Yue was very cunning and corrupt; successive defense commissioners could not control him.
translations.idiomatic: A military officer named Bai Yue was extremely cunning and corrupt; successive defense commissioners had been unable to control him.

sentences.zh: 龜因事發，笞死以徇，人皆畏威自效。

translations.literal: Gui seized on an incident to expose him, had him flogged to death as a warning, and all feared his authority and exerted themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Gui seized on an incident to expose him, had him flogged to death as a public warning, and everyone feared his authority and exerted themselves accordingly.

sentences.zh: 十四年，轉越州刺史、御史大夫、浙東團練觀察使。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Governor of Yue Prefecture, Censor-in-Chief, and Military Training Commissioner and Inspector of Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to governor of Yue Prefecture, censor-in-chief, and military training commissioner and inspector of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 先是，龜兄式撫臨此郡，有惠政；

translations.literal: Previously his elder brother Shi had governed this prefecture and had benevolent policies;
translations.idiomatic: Previously his elder brother Shi had governed this prefecture and carried out benevolent policies;

sentences.zh: 聞龜復至，舞抃迎之。

translations.literal: When they heard Gui had come again, they danced with joy to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When the people heard that Gui had come again, they danced with joy to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 屬徐、泗之亂，江淮盜起，山越亂，攻郡，為賊所害。

translations.literal: At the time of the Xu-Si rebellion, bandits rose on the Yangzi and Huai rivers; the Shanyue rebelled, attacked the prefecture, and he was killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: At the time of the Xu-Si rebellion, bandits rose throughout the Yangzi and Huai region; the Shanyue rebelled, attacked the prefecture, and Gui was killed by the bandits.

sentences.zh: 贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted minister of works.

sentences.zh: 子蕘。

translations.literal: His son was Rao.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Rao.

sentences.zh: 蕘苦學，善屬文。

translations.literal: Rao studied arduously and was skilled at composing prose.
translations.idiomatic: Rao studied arduously and was skilled at composing prose.

sentences.zh: 以季父作相，避嫌不就科試。

translations.literal: Because his younger uncle served as chief minister, he avoided suspicion and did not take the civil examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Because his younger uncle served as chief minister, he avoided suspicion and did not take the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 乾符初，崔瑾廉察湖南，崔涓鎮江陵，皆辟為從事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianfu, Cui Jin inspected Hunan and Cui Juan governed Jiangling; both recruited him as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qianfu reign, Cui Jin inspected Hunan and Cui Juan governed Jiangling; both recruited Rao as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 蕭遘作相，奏授藍田尉，直史館，遷左拾遺、右補闕，中丞盧涯奏為侍御史。

translations.literal: When Xiao Fu became chief minister, he memorialized to appoint him Magistrate of Lantian and duty Editor of the History Office; he was promoted to Left Remonstrance Clerk and Right Supplementation Clerk; Censor-in-Chief Lu Ya memorialized to make him Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Fu became chief minister, he memorialized to appoint Rao magistrate of Lantian and duty editor of the History Office; Rao was then promoted to left remonstrance clerk and right supplementation clerk, and censor-in-chief Lu Ya memorialized to make him attending censor.

sentences.zh: 從僖宗幸山南，拜右司員外郎，卒。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Xizong to Shannan, was appointed Junior Director in the Right Ministry, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Xizong to Shannan, was appointed junior director in the right ministry, and died.

sentences.zh: 子權，中興仕至兵部尚書。

translations.literal: His son Quan, during the Restoration, rose in office to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: His son Quan, during the Restoration, rose in office to minister of war.

sentences.zh: 式以門廕，累遷監察御史，轉殿中，亦巧宦。

translations.literal: Shi entered office through hereditary privilege, was promoted in succession to Censor, transferred to the Palace Administration, and was also adept at office-seeking.
translations.idiomatic: Shi entered office through hereditary privilege, rose in succession to censor, transferred to the Palace Administration, and was also a skilled careerist.

sentences.zh: 太和中，依倚鄭註，謁王守澄，為中丞歸融所劾，出為江陵少尹。

translations.literal: In Taihe, relying on Zheng Zhu, he paid court to Wang Shoucheng; censured by Censor-in-Chief Gui Rong, he was sent out as Vice Governor of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe reign, relying on Zheng Zhu, he paid court to Wang Shoucheng; censured by censor-in-chief Gui Rong, he was sent out as vice governor of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 大中後，踐更省署。

translations.literal: After Dazhong he served in succession in provincial offices.
translations.idiomatic: After the Dazhong reign he served in succession in provincial offices.

sentences.zh: 咸通初，為浙東觀察使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiantong he was Inspector of Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xiantong reign he served as inspector of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 草賊仇甫據明州叛，來攻會稽，式討平之。

translations.literal: The bandit Chou Fu occupied Ming Prefecture and rebelled, came to attack Kuaiji, and Shi suppressed and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Chou Fu seized Ming Prefecture and rebelled, then marched to attack Kuaiji; Shi suppressed and pacified him.

sentences.zh: 式有威略。

translations.literal: Shi had authority and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Shi possessed authority and strategic ability.

sentences.zh: 三年，徐州銀刀軍叛，以式為徐州節度使。

translations.literal: In the third year the Silver Blade Army of Xuzhou rebelled; Shi was made Military Commissioner of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the Silver Blade Army of Xuzhou rebelled, and Shi was made military commissioner of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 式至鎮，盡誅銀刀等七軍，徐方平定。

translations.literal: When Shi reached his command, he executed to the last man the Silver Blade and seven other armies; the Xu region was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi reached his post, he executed every man of the Silver Blade Army and six other armies; the Xu region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 天子嘉之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven commended him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him.

sentences.zh: 後累歷方任，卒。

translations.literal: Later he served in succession in regional posts, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in succession in regional posts and died.

sentences.zh: 鐸，字昭範。

translations.literal: Duo, style name Zhaofan.
translations.idiomatic: Duo, whose style name was Zhaofan.

sentences.zh: 會昌初進士第，兩辟使府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huichang he passed the jinshi examination; twice he was summoned to prefectural staff offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Huichang reign he passed the jinshi examination and was twice summoned to serve on prefectural staffs.

sentences.zh: 大中初，入為監察御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong he entered court as Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Dazhong reign he entered court as censor.

sentences.zh: 咸通初，由駕部郎中知制誥，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiantong, from Director in the Transport Bureau he took charge of drafting edicts, and was appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xiantong reign he rose from director in the Transport Bureau to take charge of drafting edicts and was appointed secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 五年，轉禮部侍郎，典貢士兩歲，時稱得人。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites; for two years he oversaw the tribute scholars, and at the time it was said he had selected the right men.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to vice minister of rites and for two years oversaw the civil examinations; at the time it was said he had chosen the right men.

sentences.zh: 七年，以戶部侍郎、判度支，遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, as Vice Minister of Revenue and concurrently director of the Transport Bureau, he was promoted to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, as vice minister of revenue and concurrently director of the transport bureau, he was promoted to minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 十二年，以本官同平章事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, with his existing office he became co-administrator of the State Affairs Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, with his existing office he became co-administrator of the State Affairs Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 時宰相韋保衡以拔擢之恩，事鐸尤謹，累兼刑部、吏部尚書。

translations.literal: At the time chief minister Wei Baoheng, owing to the kindness of having been promoted, served Duo with especial deference; Duo cumulatively also held the posts of Minister of Justice and Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At the time chief minister Wei Baoheng, owing to the kindness of having been promoted, served Duo with especial deference; Duo cumulatively also held the posts of minister of justice and minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 僖宗即位，加右僕射。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong ascended the throne, he was additionally granted Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong ascended the throne, Duo was additionally granted right vice director.

sentences.zh: 保衡得罪，以鐸檢校右僕射，出為汴州刺史、宣武軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Baoheng fell from favor, Duo was made acting Right Vice Director and sent out as prefect of Bian and military commissioner of the Xuanwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoheng fell from favor, Duo was made acting right vice director and sent out as prefect of Bian and military commissioner of the Xuanwu Army.

sentences.zh: 鐸有經世大志，以安邦為己任，士友推之。

translations.literal: Duo had great ambitions to order the age and took securing the realm as his charge; scholar-friends praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Duo had great ambitions to order the age and took securing the realm as his personal charge; scholar-friends praised him.

sentences.zh: 乾符二年，河南、江左相繼寇盜結集，內官田令孜素聞鐸名，乃復召鐸，拜右僕射、門下侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianfu, bandits and robbers gathered in succession in Henan and the lower Yangzi region; palace official Tian Lingzi, who had long heard of Duo's reputation, thereupon recalled Duo and appointed him Right Vice Director, Vice Director of the Secretariat, and co-administrator of the State Affairs Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianfu, bandits and robbers gathered in succession in Henan and the lower Yangzi region; palace official Tian Lingzi, who had long heard of Duo's reputation, thereupon recalled Duo and appointed him right vice director, vice director of the secretariat, and co-administrator of the State Affairs Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 四年，賊陷江陵，楊知溫失守，宋威破賊失策。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the rebels captured Jiangling; Yang Zhiwen lost his post; Song Wei failed in strategy to defeat the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the rebels captured Jiangling; Yang Zhiwen lost his post; and Song Wei failed in his strategy to defeat the rebels.

sentences.zh: 朝議統率，宰相盧攜稱高駢累立戰功，宜付軍柄，物議未允。

translations.literal: At court there was discussion of overall command; chief minister Lu Xie said Gao Pian had repeatedly established battle merit and ought to be entrusted with military authority, but public opinion did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: At court there was discussion of overall command; chief minister Lu Xie said Gao Pian had repeatedly established battle merit and ought to be entrusted with military authority, but public opinion did not approve.

sentences.zh: 鐸廷奏曰：「臣忝宰執之長，在朝不足分陛下之憂。

translations.literal: Duo memorialized at court, saying: "Your subject, who shamefully holds the chief place among chief ministers, in court is insufficient to share Your Majesty's worries.
translations.idiomatic: Duo memorialized at court, saying: "Your subject, who shamefully holds the chief place among chief ministers, at court is insufficient to share Your Majesty's worries.

sentences.zh: 臣願自率諸軍，蕩滌群盜。」

translations.literal: Your subject wishes to lead the armies himself and sweep away the band of robbers.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject wishes to lead the armies himself and sweep away the band of robbers.

sentences.zh: 朝議然之。

translations.literal: Court discussion approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Court discussion approved of this.

sentences.zh: 五年，以鐸守司徒、門下侍郎、同平章事，兼江陵尹、荊南節度使，充諸道行營兵馬都統。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Duo was made Honorary Grand Preceptor, Vice Director of the Secretariat, and co-administrator of the State Affairs Chancellery, concurrently governor of Jiangling and military commissioner of Jingnan, and appointed overall commander of the field armies and cavalry of all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Duo was made honorary grand preceptor, vice director of the secretariat, and co-administrator of the State Affairs Chancellery, concurrently governor of Jiangling and military commissioner of Jingnan, and appointed overall commander of the field armies and cavalry of all circuits.

sentences.zh: 鐸至鎮，綏懷流散，完葺軍戎，期年之間，武備嚴整。

translations.literal: When Duo reached his command, he soothed and gathered the scattered, repaired the army, and within a year military preparations were strict and in order.
translations.idiomatic: When Duo reached his post, he soothed and gathered the scattered population, repaired the army, and within a year military preparations were strict and in order.

sentences.zh: 時兗州節度使李系者，西平王晟之孫，以其家世將才，奏用為都統都押衙，兼湘南團練使。

translations.literal: At the time the military commissioner of Yan was Li Xi, grandson of King Sheng of Xiping; because of his family's hereditary military talent, Duo memorialized to employ him as chief adjutant of the overall commander, concurrently regimental commissioner of southern Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the military commissioner of Yan was Li Xi, grandson of King Sheng of Xiping; because of his family's hereditary military talent, Duo memorialized to employ him as chief adjutant of the overall commander, concurrently regimental commissioner of southern Hunan.

sentences.zh: 時黃巢在嶺南，鐸悉以精甲付系，令分兵扼嶺路。

translations.literal: At the time Huang Chao was in Lingnan; Duo entrusted all his elite armor to Xi and ordered him to divide troops and block the mountain passes.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Huang Chao was in Lingnan; Duo entrusted all his elite troops to Xi and ordered him to divide his forces and block the mountain passes.

sentences.zh: 系無將略，微有口才，軍政不理。

translations.literal: Xi lacked military strategy, had a slight gift for speech, and did not administer army affairs properly.
translations.idiomatic: Xi lacked military strategy, had a slight gift for speech, and did not administer army affairs properly.

sentences.zh: 廣明初，賊自嶺南寇湖南諸郡，系守城自固，不敢出戰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangming the rebels from Lingnan raided the various prefectures of Hunan; Xi held the city and fortified himself, not daring to go out to battle.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Guangming reign the rebels from Lingnan raided the various prefectures of Hunan; Xi held the city and fortified himself, not daring to go out to battle.

sentences.zh: 賊編木為伐，沿湘而下，急攻潭州，陷之。

translations.literal: The rebels bound logs into rafts, went down the Xiang River, urgently attacked Tanzhou, and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels bound logs into rafts, went down the Xiang River, urgently attacked Tanzhou, and captured it.

sentences.zh: 系甲兵五萬，皆為賊所殺，投屍於江。

translations.literal: Xi's fifty thousand armored troops were all killed by the rebels, and corpses were thrown into the river.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's fifty thousand armored troops were all killed by the rebels, and their corpses were thrown into the river.

sentences.zh: 鐸聞系敗，令部將董漢宏守江陵，自率兵萬余會襄陽之師。

translations.literal: When Duo heard of Xi's defeat, he ordered his officer Dong Hanhong to hold Jiangling and personally led more than ten thousand troops to join the forces from Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Duo heard of Xi's defeat, he ordered his officer Dong Hanhong to hold Jiangling and personally led more than ten thousand troops to join the forces from Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 江陵竟陷於賊。

translations.literal: Jiangling ultimately fell to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangling ultimately fell to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 天子不之責。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven did not hold him accountable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not hold him accountable.

sentences.zh: 罷相，守太子太師。

translations.literal: He was removed as chief minister and made Honorary Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed as chief minister and made honorary grand mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 宰相盧攜用事，竟以淮南高駢代鐸為都統。

translations.literal: Chief minister Lu Xie held power, and in the end Gao Pian of Huainan replaced Duo as overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Lu Xie held power, and in the end Gao Pian of Huainan replaced Duo as overall commander.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，賊焚剽淮南，高駢挫敗。

translations.literal: That autumn the rebels burned and plundered Huainan, and Gao Pian suffered defeats.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the rebels burned and plundered Huainan, and Gao Pian suffered defeats.

sentences.zh: 及賊陷兩京，盧攜得罪，天子用鄭畋為兵馬都統。

translations.literal: When the rebels captured the two capitals, Lu Xie fell from favor, and the Son of Heaven employed Zheng Tian as overall commander of armies and cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels captured the two capitals, Lu Xie fell from favor, and the emperor employed Zheng Tian as overall commander of armies and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 明年，畋病歸行在，朝議復以鐸為侍中、滑州刺史、義成軍節度使，充諸道行營都統。

translations.literal: The next year Tian fell ill and returned to the imperial camp; court discussion again made Duo Palace Secretary, prefect of Hua, military commissioner of the Yicheng Army, and overall commander of the field headquarters of all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Tian fell ill and returned to the imperial camp; court discussion again made Duo palace secretary, prefect of Hua, military commissioner of the Yicheng Army, and overall commander of the field headquarters of all circuits.

sentences.zh: 率禁軍、山南、東蜀之師三萬，營於盩厔東，進屯靈感寺。

translations.literal: He led thirty thousand troops of the imperial guard, Shannan, and eastern Shu, encamped east of Zhouzhi, and advanced to garrison at Linggan Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He led thirty thousand troops of the imperial guard, Shannan, and eastern Shu, encamped east of Zhouzhi, and advanced to garrison at Linggan Temple.

sentences.zh: 明年春，兗、鄆、徐、許、鄭、滑、邠、寧、鳳翔十鎮之師大集關內。

translations.literal: The next spring the armies of the ten commands—Yan, Yun, Xu, Xu, Zheng, Hua, Bin, Ning, and Fengxiang—massed greatly within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring the armies of the ten commands—Yan, Yun, Xu, Xu, Zheng, Hua, Bin, Ning, and Fengxiang—massed greatly within the passes.

sentences.zh: 時賊已僭名號；

translations.literal: At the time the rebels had already usurped titles;
translations.idiomatic: At the time the rebels had already usurped titles;

sentences.zh: 以前漸東觀察使崔璆、尚讓為宰相，傳偽命。
