translations.literal: They made former Zhedong inspector Cui Qiu and Shang Rang chief ministers and disseminated false edicts.
translations.idiomatic: They made former Zhedong inspector Cui Qiu and Shang Rang chief ministers and disseminated false edicts.

sentences.zh: 天下籓帥，多持兩端。

translations.literal: Military commissioners throughout the realm mostly hedged between two sides.
translations.idiomatic: Military commissioners throughout the realm mostly hedged between two sides.

sentences.zh: 既聞鐸傳檄四方，諸侯翻然景附。

translations.literal: Once they heard Duo circulate proclamations to the four quarters, the feudal lords suddenly turned to follow him as if drawn to his brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: Once they heard Duo circulate proclamations to the four quarters, the feudal lords suddenly turned to follow him as if drawn to his brilliance.

sentences.zh: 賊之號令，東西不過岐、華，南北止及山、河。

translations.literal: The rebels' orders extended east-west no farther than Qi and Hua, and north-south only as far as the mountains and the river.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels' orders extended east-west no farther than Qi and Hua, and north-south only as far as the mountains and the river.

sentences.zh: 而勁卒驍將，日馳突於國門，群賊由是離心。

translations.literal: Yet elite troops and fierce generals daily galloped and raided at the capital gates, and the band of rebels thereby lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yet elite troops and fierce generals daily galloped and raided at the capital gates, and the band of rebels thereby lost heart.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，賊將硃溫降，收同州。

translations.literal: That autumn the rebel general Zhu Wen surrendered, and Tongzhou was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the rebel general Zhu Wen surrendered, and Tongzhou was recovered.

sentences.zh: 十一月，賊華州戍卒七千來奔。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month seven thousand garrison troops of Hua from the rebels came over to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month seven thousand garrison troops of Hua from the rebels came over to surrender.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，沙陀軍至，收華州。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year the Shatuo army arrived and recovered Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year the Shatuo army arrived and recovered Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 四月，敗賊於良田坡，遂收京城。

translations.literal: In the fourth month they defeated the rebels at Liangtian Slope and thereupon recovered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month they defeated the rebels at Liangtian Slope and thereupon recovered the capital.

sentences.zh: 封鐸晉國公。

translations.literal: Duo was enfeoffed as Duke of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Duo was enfeoffed as Duke of Jin.

sentences.zh: 鐸加中書令，以收城諸將，量其功伐高下，承制爵賞以聞。

translations.literal: Duo was additionally made Director of the Secretariat; regarding the generals who recovered the city, he measured their merits as high or low and, by imperial commission, reported enfeoffments and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Duo was additionally made director of the secretariat; regarding the generals who recovered the city, he measured their merits as high or low and, by imperial commission, reported enfeoffments and rewards.

sentences.zh: 是時國命危若綴旒，天子播越蠻陬，大事去矣。

translations.literal: At this time the fate of the state hung by a thread, the Son of Heaven wandered to barbarian frontiers, and the great enterprise was nearly lost.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the fate of the state hung by a thread, the emperor wandered to barbarian frontiers, and the great enterprise was nearly lost.

sentences.zh: 若非鄭畋之奮發，鐸之忠義，則土運之隆替，未可知也。

translations.literal: Had it not been for Zheng Tian's vigorous action and Duo's loyalty and righteousness, whether the dynasty's fortune would rise or fall would have been impossible to know.
translations.idiomatic: Had it not been for Zheng Tian's vigorous action and Duo's loyalty and righteousness, whether the dynasty's fortune would rise or fall would have been impossible to know.

sentences.zh: 自巢、讓之亂，關東方鎮牙將，皆逐主帥，自號籓臣。

translations.literal: Since the turmoil of Chao and Rang, garrison adjutants in the eastern passes region all drove out their commanders and styled themselves as vassal officials.
translations.idiomatic: Since the turmoil of Chao and Rang, garrison adjutants in the eastern passes region all drove out their commanders and styled themselves as vassal officials.

sentences.zh: 時溥據徐州，硃瑄據鄆州，硃瑾據兗州，王敬武據青州，周岌據許州，王重榮據河中，諸葛爽據河陽，皆自擅一籓，職貢不入，賞罰由己。

translations.literal: Shi Pu held Xuzhou, Zhu Xuan held Yunzhou, Zhu Jin held Yanzhou, Wang Jingwu held Qingzhou, Zhou Ji held Xuzhou, Wang Chongrong held Hezhong, and Zhuge Shuang held Heyang—all arrogated a province to themselves, did not send tribute and reports to court, and imposed rewards and punishments on their own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu held Xuzhou, Zhu Xuan held Yunzhou, Zhu Jin held Yanzhou, Wang Jingwu held Qingzhou, Zhou Ji held Xuzhou, Wang Chongrong held Hezhong, and Zhuge Shuang held Heyang—all arrogated a province to themselves, did not send tribute and reports to court, and imposed rewards and punishments on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 既逐賊出關，尤恃功伐，朝廷姑息不暇。

translations.literal: Having driven the rebels out of the passes, they especially relied on their merits and victories; the court had no time to do more than indulgent accommodation.
translations.idiomatic: Having driven the rebels out of the passes, they especially relied on their merits and victories; the court had no time to do more than indulgent accommodation.

sentences.zh: 巢賊出關東，與蔡帥秦宗權合縱。

translations.literal: Chao's rebels went out east of the passes and joined in coalition with Qin Zongquan, commandery chief of Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Chao's rebels went out east of the passes and joined in coalition with Qin Zongquan, commandery chief of Cai.

sentences.zh: 時溥舉兵徐方，請身先討賊，乃授溥都統之命。

translations.literal: Shi Pu raised troops in the Xu region, requested to take the lead in attacking the rebels, and thereupon was granted the order of overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu raised troops in the Xu region, requested to take the lead in attacking the rebels, and thereupon was granted the order of overall commander.

sentences.zh: 十軍軍容使田令孜，以內官楊復光有監護用師之功，尤忌儒臣立事，故有時溥之授。

translations.literal: Tian Lingzi, commissioner of the Ten Armies' military bearing, because palace official Yang Fuguang had merit in supervising and deploying the army, especially resented civil officials achieving things, and therefore there was the appointment of Shi Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi, commissioner of the Ten Armies' military bearing, because palace official Yang Fuguang had merit in supervising and deploying the army, especially resented civil officials achieving things, and therefore there was the appointment of Shi Pu.

sentences.zh: 初，鐸出軍，兼鄭滑節度使，以便供饋。

translations.literal: Initially, when Duo marched out with the army, he also held the post of military commissioner of Zheng and Hua to facilitate provisioning.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, when Duo marched out with the army, he also held the post of military commissioner of Zheng and Hua to facilitate provisioning.

sentences.zh: 至是，罷鐸都統之權，令仗節歸籓。

translations.literal: At this point Duo's authority as overall commander was removed, and he was ordered to return to his province bearing his credential.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Duo's authority as overall commander was removed, and he was ordered to return to his province bearing his credential.

sentences.zh: 鐸以硃全忠於己有恩，倚為籓蔽。

translations.literal: Duo felt Zhu Quanzhong owed him a kindness and relied on him as a border shield.
translations.idiomatic: Duo felt Zhu Quanzhong owed him a kindness and relied on him as a border shield.

sentences.zh: 初，全忠辭禮恭順，既而全忠軍旅稍集，其意漸倨。

translations.literal: At first Quanzhong's words and courtesy were deferential; afterward, as Quanzhong's armies gradually gathered, his attitude grew gradually arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: At first Quanzhong's words and courtesy were deferential; afterward, as Quanzhong's armies gradually gathered, his attitude grew gradually arrogant.

sentences.zh: 鐸知不可依，表求還朝。

translations.literal: Duo knew he could not rely on him and memorialized requesting return to court.
translations.idiomatic: Duo knew he could not rely on him and memorialized requesting return to court.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，僖宗自蜀將還，乃以鐸為滄景節度使。

translations.literal: That winter, as Emperor Xizong was about to return from Shu, Duo was made military commissioner of Cang and Jing.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, as Emperor Xizong was about to return from Shu, Duo was made military commissioner of Cang and Jing.

sentences.zh: 時楊全玫在滄州，聞鐸之來，訴於魏州樂彥貞。

translations.literal: At the time Yang Quanmei was at Cangzhou; hearing of Duo's coming, he appealed to Le Yan Zhen at Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yang Quanmei was at Cangzhou; hearing of Duo's coming, he appealed to Le Yan Zhen at Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 鐸受命赴鎮，至魏州旬日，彥貞迎謁，宴勞甚至。

translations.literal: Duo received the order and went to his command; after ten days at Weizhou, Yan Zhen came to meet and welcome him and entertained and rewarded him with exceptional generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Duo received the order and went to his post; after ten days at Weizhou, Yan Zhen came to meet and welcome him and entertained and rewarded him with exceptional generosity.

sentences.zh: 鐸以上臺元老，功蓋群後，行則肩輿，妓女夾侍，賓僚服禦，盡美一時。

translations.literal: Duo, as an elder of the supreme court whose achievements surpassed all his peers, traveled in a shoulder-borne carriage with singing girls attending on either side, guests and staff arrayed in finery—the utmost splendor of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Duo, as an elder of the supreme court whose achievements surpassed all his peers, traveled in a shoulder-borne carriage with singing girls attending on either side, guests and staff arrayed in finery—the utmost splendor of the age.

sentences.zh: 彥貞子從訓，兇戾無行，竊所慕之；

translations.literal: Yan Zhen's son Congxun, violent and without propriety, secretly coveted this;
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhen's son Congxun, violent and without propriety, secretly coveted this;

sentences.zh: 令甘陵州卒數百人，伏於漳南之高雞泊。

translations.literal: He had several hundred soldiers from Ganling Prefecture lie in ambush at Gaojibo south of the Zhang River.
translations.idiomatic: He had several hundred soldiers from Ganling Prefecture lie in ambush at Gaojibo south of the Zhang River.

sentences.zh: 及鐸行李至，皆為所掠，鐸與賓客十余人，皆遇害。

translations.literal: When Duo's baggage train arrived, all were plundered; Duo and more than ten guests all met violent death.
translations.idiomatic: When Duo's baggage train arrived, all were plundered; Duo and more than ten guests all met violent death.

sentences.zh: 時光啟四年十二月也。

translations.literal: This was in the twelfth month of the fourth year of Guangqi.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the twelfth month of the fourth year of Guangqi.

sentences.zh: 鐸弟鐐，累官至汝州刺史。

translations.literal: Duo's younger brother Liao rose in office to prefect of Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Duo's younger brother Liao rose in office to prefect of Ru.

sentences.zh: 王仙芝陷郡城，被害。

translations.literal: When Wang Xianzhi captured the prefectural city, he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Xianzhi captured the prefectural city, he was killed.

sentences.zh: 李絳，字深之，趙郡贊皇人也。

translations.literal: Li Jiang, Li Jiang, style name Shenzhi, a native of Zanhuang in Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang, whose style name was Shenzhi, was a native of Zanhuang in Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖貞簡。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather was Zhenjian.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather was Zhenjian.

sentences.zh: 祖剛，官終宰邑。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gang ended his office as magistrate of a district.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gang ended his office as magistrate of a district.

sentences.zh: 父元善，襄州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: His father Yuanshan was administrative aide of Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuanshan served as administrative aide of Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 絳舉進士，登宏辭科，授秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: Jiang passed the jinshi examination, passed the macro-literary examination, and was appointed collator in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang passed the jinshi examination, passed the macro-literary examination, and was appointed collator in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，補渭南尉。

translations.literal: When his term expired he was appointed chief warden of Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he was appointed chief warden of Weinan.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenyuan he was appointed Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenyuan reign he was appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 元和二年，以本官充翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhe, with his existing office he was appointed Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanhe, with his existing office he was appointed Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改尚書主客員外郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to junior director in the Ministry of Rites in charge of foreign visitors.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was changed to junior director in the Ministry of Rites in charge of foreign visitors.

sentences.zh: 逾年，轉司勛員外郎。

translations.literal: After a year he was transferred to junior director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was transferred to junior director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷本司郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to director in that ministry and took charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to director in that ministry and took charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 皆不離內職，孜孜以匡諫為己任。

translations.literal: Throughout he did not leave inner court duties, diligently taking remonstrance and correction as his charge.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout he did not leave inner court duties, diligently taking remonstrance and correction as his personal charge.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，叛臣李锜阻兵於浙右。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong ascended the throne, the rebel Li Qi blocked the army in Zheyou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong ascended the throne, the rebel Li Qi blocked the army in Zheyou.

sentences.zh: 锜既誅，朝廷將輦其所沒家財。

translations.literal: Once Qi was executed, the court was about to transport by cart his confiscated family property.
translations.idiomatic: Once Qi was executed, the court was about to transport by cart his confiscated family property.

sentences.zh: 絳上言曰：「李锜兇狡叛戾，僭侈誅求，刻剝六州之人，積成一道之苦。

translations.literal: Jiang memorialized, saying: "Li Qi was vicious, cunning, rebellious, and perverse; he usurped extravagance and imposed exactions, flaying the people of six prefectures and heaping up the suffering of an entire circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang memorialized, saying: "Li Qi was vicious, cunning, rebellious, and perverse; he usurped extravagance and imposed exactions, flaying the people of six prefectures and heaping up the suffering of an entire circuit.

sentences.zh: 聖恩本以叛亂致討，蘇息一方。

translations.literal: The sage grace originally took rebellion as cause for punitive action, to revive and rest one region.
translations.idiomatic: The sage grace originally took rebellion as cause for punitive action, to revive and rest one region.

sentences.zh: 今輦運錢帛，播聞四海，非所謂式遏亂略，惠綏困窮。

translations.literal: Now transporting money and silks by cart, broadcasting the news to the four seas—this is not what is called checking disorder and raids, or showing kindness and ease to the destitute.
translations.idiomatic: Now transporting money and silks by cart, broadcasting the news to the four seas—this is not what is called checking disorder and raids, or showing kindness and ease to the destitute.

sentences.zh: 伏望天慈，並賜本道，代貧下戶今年租稅，則萬姓欣戴，四海歌詠矣。」

translations.literal: I humbly hope for heavenly kindness: grant it all to this circuit in place of this year's tax and rent for poor households, and then the myriad people will rejoice and look up in gratitude, and the four seas will sing in praise.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope for heavenly kindness: grant it all to this circuit in place of this year's tax and rent for poor households, and then the myriad people will rejoice and look up in gratitude, and the four seas will sing in praise.

sentences.zh: 憲宗嘉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong commended this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong commended this.

sentences.zh: 時中官吐突承璀自籓邸承恩寵，為神策護軍中尉，乃於安國佛寺建立《聖政碑》，大興功作，仍請翰林為其文。

translations.literal: At the time palace official Tuoba Chenghui, favored from the princely residence, was protector-general commandant of the Shence Army; he thereupon erected the "Stele of Sagely Governance" at Anguo Temple, launched great construction works, and still requested the Hanlin to compose its text.
translations.idiomatic: At the time palace official Tuoba Chenghui, favored from the princely residence, was protector-general commandant of the Shence Army; he thereupon erected the "Stele of Sagely Governance" at Anguo Temple, launched great construction works, and still requested the Hanlin to compose its text.

sentences.zh: 絳上言曰：

translations.literal: Jiang memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Jiang memorialized, saying:

sentences.zh: 陛下布惟新之政，刬積習之弊，四海延頸，日望德音。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has promulgated renewing policies and cut away the evils of accumulated custom; the four seas stretch their necks, daily awaiting virtuous words.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has promulgated renewing policies and cut away the evils of accumulated custom; the four seas stretch their necks, daily awaiting virtuous words.

sentences.zh: 今忽立《聖政碑》，示天下以不廣。

translations.literal: Now suddenly to erect the "Stele of Sagely Governance" shows the realm your lack of magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Now suddenly to erect the "Stele of Sagely Governance" shows the realm your lack of magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 《易》稱：大人者與天地合德，與日月合明。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: the great man merges his virtue with Heaven and Earth and his brilliance with sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: the great man merges his virtue with Heaven and Earth and his brilliance with sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 執契垂拱，勵精求理，豈可以文字而盡聖德，碑表而贊皇猷？

translations.literal: Holding the tally and ruling without effort, striving in spirit to seek good order—how can sage virtue be exhausted in words, or imperial design praised on a stele?
translations.idiomatic: Holding the tally and ruling without effort, striving in spirit to seek good order—how can sage virtue be exhausted in words, or imperial design praised on a stele?

sentences.zh: 若可敘述，是有分限，虧損盛德，豈謂敷揚至道哉？

translations.literal: If it can be narrated, there is a limit to it; to do so diminishes sublime virtue—how can this be called spreading and displaying the utmost Way?
translations.idiomatic: If it can be narrated, there is a limit to it; to do so diminishes sublime virtue—how can this be called spreading and displaying the utmost Way?

sentences.zh: 故自堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武，並無建碑之事。

translations.literal: Therefore from Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, none had steles erected.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore from Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, none had steles erected.

sentences.zh: 至秦始皇荒逸之君，煩酷之政，然後有罘、嶧之碑，揚誅伐之功，紀巡幸之跡，適足為百王所笑，萬代所譏。

translations.literal: Only when it came to Qin Shihuang, a dissolute ruler with oppressive government, were there the steles at Mount Fu and Mount Yi, proclaiming punitive campaigns and recording tour itineraries—fit only to be laughed at by the hundred kings and mocked through ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Only when it came to Qin Shihuang, a dissolute ruler with oppressive government, were there the steles at Mount Fu and Mount Yi, proclaiming punitive campaigns and recording tour itineraries—fit only to be laughed at by the hundred kings and mocked through ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 至今稱為失道亡國之主，豈可擬議於此！

translations.literal: To this day he is called a ruler who lost the Way and destroyed his state—how can one compare and discuss such a thing here!
translations.idiomatic: To this day he is remembered as a ruler who lost the Way and destroyed his kingdom—how can Your Majesty be compared to him in this!

sentences.zh: 陛下嗣高祖、太宗之業，舉貞觀、開元之政，思理不遑食，從諫如順流；

translations.literal: Your Majesty inherits the enterprise of Gaozu and Taizong, upholds the governance of the Zhenguan and Kaiyuan eras, thinks of good order without leisure to eat, and accepts remonstrance as if going with the current;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty inherits the legacy of Gaozu and Taizong, upholds the policies of the Zhenguan and Kaiyuan eras, pursues good governance without pausing even to eat, and accepts remonstrance as readily as water flows downstream;

sentences.zh: 固可與堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武方駕而行，又安得追秦皇暴虐不經之事，而自損聖政？

translations.literal: Surely you can walk abreast with Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu—how then can you follow the brutal and unprincipled deeds of Qin Shihuang and diminish your own sage governance?
translations.idiomatic: Surely you can walk in the company of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu—how then can you emulate the brutal and lawless conduct of the First Emperor of Qin and diminish your own sage rule?

sentences.zh: 近者，閻巨源請立紀聖功碑，陛下詳盡事宜，皆不允許。

translations.literal: Recently Yan Juyuan requested erecting a stele recording sage achievements; Your Majesty examined the matter in full and did not permit any of it.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Yan Juyuan petitioned to erect a stele commemorating Your Majesty's sage achievements; Your Majesty reviewed the proposal in detail and refused it entirely.

sentences.zh: 今忽令立此，與前事頗乖。

translations.literal: Now suddenly ordering this erected is quite at odds with what went before.
translations.idiomatic: Now suddenly ordering this stele erected is quite inconsistent with what went before.

sentences.zh: 況此碑既在安國寺，不得不敘載遊觀宗飾之事。

translations.literal: Moreover, since this stele would stand at Anguo Temple, one could not avoid narrating matters of sightseeing and adornment of the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since this stele would stand at Anguo Temple, its inscription could hardly avoid recounting sightseeing and the temple's ornamental splendor.

sentences.zh: 述遊觀且乖理要，敘崇飾又匪政經，固非哲王所宜行也。

translations.literal: To describe sightseeing departs from essential principle; to narrate grand adornment is not the norm of governance—it is certainly not what a wise king should do.
translations.idiomatic: To describe sightseeing departs from what is essential; to narrate grand ornamentation is not the standard of governance—it is certainly not what a wise ruler should do.

sentences.zh: 其碑，伏乞聖恩特令寢罷。

translations.literal: As for this stele, I humbly beg your sage grace specially to order it suspended and abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: As for this stele, I humbly beg Your Majesty's grace to order it specially suspended and abandoned.

sentences.zh: 憲宗深然之，其碑遂止。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong deeply agreed; the stele was then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong strongly agreed, and the stele project was halted.

sentences.zh: 絳後因浴堂北廊奏對，極論中官縱恣、方鎮進獻之事。

translations.literal: Later Jiang presented a response in the north corridor of the Bathing Hall, exhaustively discussing the unrestrained conduct of inner officials and the tribute offerings of regional commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Later, during an audience in the north corridor of the Bathing Hall, Jiang spoke at length about the unrestrained conduct of eunuch officials and the tribute offerings of the regional commanders.

sentences.zh: 憲宗怒，厲聲曰：「卿所論奏，何太過耶？」

translations.literal: Xianzong grew angry and said sharply: "What you have presented in discussion—is it not excessive?"
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong grew angry and said sharply, "What you have presented—is it not excessive?"

sentences.zh: 絳前論不已，曰：「臣所諫論，於臣無利，是國家之利。

translations.literal: Jiang continued advancing his argument without stop and said: "What I remonstrate about brings no profit to me—it is profit to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang pressed on without stopping and said, "What I remonstrate about brings me no personal benefit—it is benefit to the state.

sentences.zh: 陛下不以臣愚，使處腹心之地，豈可見事虧聖德，致損清時，而惜身不言？

translations.literal: Your Majesty, not deeming me foolish, placed me in a position of inner trust—how could I see affairs that diminish sage virtue and injure this bright age, yet spare myself and not speak?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, not deeming me foolish, placed me in a position of inner trust—how could I see affairs that diminish Your Majesty's virtue and harm this bright age, yet hold my tongue to spare myself?

sentences.zh: 仰屋竊嘆，是臣負陛下也。

translations.literal: To look up at the roof and sigh in secret—that would mean I have failed Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: To look up at the roof and sigh in secret would mean that I had failed Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 若不顧患禍，盡誠奏論，旁忤幸臣，上犯聖旨，以此獲罪，是陛下負臣也。

translations.literal: If without regard for disaster I set forth my views with full sincerity, offending favored ministers on the side and transgressing the imperial will, and for this receive punishment—that would mean Your Majesty has failed me.
translations.idiomatic: If, without regard for disaster, I speak my mind with full sincerity, offend favored ministers and transgress the imperial will, and for that am punished—that would mean Your Majesty had failed me.

sentences.zh: 且臣與中官，素不相識，又無嫌隙，只是威福太盛，上損聖朝，臣所以不敢不論耳。

translations.literal: Moreover, I and the inner officials have never known each other and bear no grudge—it is only that their power and favors are too great, to the injury of the sacred court; that is why I dare not fail to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, I have never known the eunuch officials and bear them no personal grudge—it is only that their power and privilege are too great and injure the court; that is why I dare not remain silent.

sentences.zh: 使臣緘默，非社稷之福也。」

translations.literal: To have me keep silent is no blessing to the altars of soil and grain."
translations.idiomatic: To have me keep silent would be no blessing to the state."

sentences.zh: 憲宗見其誠切，改容慰喻之曰：「卿盡節於朕，人所難言者，卿悉言之，使朕聞所不聞，真忠正誠節之臣也。

translations.literal: Xianzong saw his sincerity and changed expression to comfort and instruct him: "You have given full loyalty to me—what others find hard to say, you have all said, enabling me to hear what I had not heard. A truly loyal, upright, and sincere minister.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong saw his sincerity, changed expression, and comforted him, saying, "You have given your full loyalty to me—what others find hard to say, you have said it all, enabling me to hear what I had never heard before. You are a truly loyal, upright, and sincere minister.

sentences.zh: 他日南面，亦須如此。」

translations.literal: On other days when facing south, you must likewise do so."
translations.idiomatic: On other days when you attend court, you must speak just as frankly."

sentences.zh: 絳拜恩而退。

translations.literal: Jiang bowed in thanks and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang bowed in gratitude and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遽宣宰臣，令與改官，乃授中書舍人，依前翰林學士。

translations.literal: Immediately the chief ministers were summoned and ordered to change his office; he was appointed Secretariat Drafter, retaining his former post as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately summoned the chief ministers and ordered Jiang's office changed; he was appointed Secretariat Drafter while retaining his former post as Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 翌日，面賜金紫，帝親為絳擇良笏賜之。

translations.literal: The next day he was personally granted gold and purple in audience; the emperor personally selected a fine court tablet for Jiang and bestowed it.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor personally granted him gold and purple insignia in audience and personally selected a fine court tablet for Jiang and bestowed it.

sentences.zh: 前後朝臣裴武、柳公綽、白居易等，或為奸人所排陷，特加貶黜；

translations.literal: Before and after, court ministers such as Pei Wu, Liu Gongchuo, and Bai Juyi were at times framed by villains and specially subjected to demotion and dismissal;
translations.idiomatic: From time to time court ministers such as Pei Wu, Liu Gongchuo, and Bai Juyi were framed by villains and specially demoted or dismissed;

sentences.zh: 絳每以密疏申論，皆獲寬宥。

translations.literal: Jiang each time argued the case in secret memorials, and all obtained leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang each time pleaded their cases in secret memorials, and all obtained leniency.

sentences.zh: 及鎮州節度使王士真死，朝廷將用兵討除，絳深陳以為未可。

translations.literal: When Wang Shizhen, military governor of Zhenzhou, died and the court was about to use troops to suppress and remove [his successor], Jiang expounded deeply that it was not yet feasible.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shizhen, military governor of Zhenzhou, died and the court was about to use troops to suppress and remove his domain, Jiang argued at length that this was not yet advisable.

sentences.zh: 絳既盡心匡益，帝每有詢訪，多協事機。

translations.literal: Since Jiang had devoted his heart to assisting and benefiting [the throne], whenever the emperor inquired of him, [his answers] mostly accorded with the timing of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jiang had devoted himself wholeheartedly to assisting the throne, whenever the emperor consulted him, his counsel mostly accorded with what the situation required.

sentences.zh: 六年，猶以中人之故，罷學士，守戶部侍郎，判本司事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, still because of the eunuchs' [influence], he was removed as academician, retained as Vice Minister of Revenue, and directed affairs of that ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, still because of the eunuchs, he was removed as Hanlin Academician, retained as Vice Minister of Revenue, and directed affairs of that ministry.

sentences.zh: 嘗因次對，憲宗曰：「戶部比有進獻，至卿獨無，何也？」

translations.literal: Once during a secondary audience, Xianzong said: "The Ministry of Revenue lately has made presentations; only you have made none—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Once during a secondary audience, Xianzong said, "The Ministry of Revenue has lately been making presentations to me, yet you alone have made none—why?"

sentences.zh: 絳曰：「將戶部錢獻入內藏，是用物以結私恩。」

translations.literal: Jiang said: "To present Ministry of Revenue funds into the inner treasury is to use material goods to forge private favor."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang said, "To present Ministry of Revenue funds into the inner treasury is to use public goods to cultivate private favor."

sentences.zh: 上聳然，益嘉其直。

translations.literal: The emperor started in surprise and all the more praised his frankness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started in surprise and all the more praised his frankness.

sentences.zh: 吐突承璀恩寵莫二，是歲，將用絳為宰相；

translations.literal: Tu Tu Chenghui's favor and grace were second to none; that year [the emperor] was about to appoint Jiang as chief minister;
translations.idiomatic: Tu Tu Chenghui's favor was unrivaled; that year the emperor was about to appoint Jiang chief minister;

sentences.zh: 前一日，出承璀為淮南監軍。

translations.literal: The day before, Chenghui was sent out as army supervisor of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, Chenghui was sent out as army supervisor of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 翌日，降制，以絳為中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: The next day an edict was issued appointing Jiang Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next day an edict was issued appointing Jiang Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 同列李吉甫便僻，善逢迎上意；

translations.literal: His colleague Li Jifu was ingratiating and skilled at accommodating the emperor's wishes;
translations.idiomatic: His colleague Li Jifu was ingratiating and skilled at accommodating the emperor's wishes;

sentences.zh: 絳梗直，多所規諫，故與吉甫不協。

translations.literal: Jiang was blunt and upright and often remonstrated; therefore he did not get along with Jifu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang was blunt and upright and often remonstrated, so he did not get along with Jifu.

sentences.zh: 時議者以吉甫通於承璀，故絳尤惡之。

translations.literal: Opinion at the time held that Jifu was connected with Chenghui; therefore Jiang especially despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion held that Jifu was connected with Chenghui, so Jiang especially despised him.

sentences.zh: 絳性剛訐，每與吉甫爭論，人多直絳。

translations.literal: Jiang's nature was stern and contentious; each time he debated with Jifu, most people sided with Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang's nature was stern and contentious; whenever he debated with Jifu, most people sided with Jiang.

sentences.zh: 憲宗察絳忠正自立，故絳論奏，多所允從。

translations.literal: Xianzong perceived that Jiang was loyal, upright, and independent; therefore Jiang's presentations were often approved and followed.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong perceived that Jiang was loyal, upright, and independent, so his memorials and presentations were often approved and followed.

sentences.zh: 上嘗謂絳曰：「卜筮之事，習者罕精，或中或否。

translations.literal: The emperor once said to Jiang: "In matters of divination by tortoise shell and yarrow stalks, those who practice it are rarely skilled—it hits or misses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said to Jiang, "In matters of divination, those who practice it are rarely skilled—the results may hit or miss.

sentences.zh: 近日風俗，

translations.literal: Recently customs [regarding this],
translations.idiomatic: Yet lately custom

sentences.zh: 尤更崇尚，何也？」

translations.literal: are even more reverenced—why?"
translations.idiomatic: has grown even more reverent toward it—why?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣聞古先哲王畏天命，示不敢專，邦有大事可疑者，故先謀於卿士庶人，次決於卜筮，俱協則行之。

translations.literal: [He] replied: "I have heard that the sage kings of antiquity feared Heaven's mandate and showed they dared not act on their own; when the state had a great matter that was doubtful, they therefore first consulted ministers and common people, next decided by divination—if all agreed, they carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I have heard that the sage kings of antiquity feared Heaven's mandate and showed that they dared not decide alone; when the state faced a great and doubtful matter, they first consulted ministers and common people, then decided by divination—and only if all agreed did they act.

sentences.zh: 末俗浮偽，幸以僥福。

translations.literal: Decadent custom is shallow and false, hoping for fortune by chance.
translations.idiomatic: Decadent custom is shallow and false, hoping for fortune by chance alone.

sentences.zh: 正行慮危，邪謀覬安，遲疑昏惑，謂小數能決之。

translations.literal: Those on the right path fear danger; those with wicked designs covet safety—in delay, doubt, and bewilderment they think petty calculations can decide things.
translations.idiomatic: Those on the right path fear danger; those with wicked designs covet safety—in hesitation, doubt, and confusion they think petty calculations can decide everything.

sentences.zh: 而愚夫愚婦，假時日鬼神者，欲利欺詐，參之見聞，用以刺射小近之事，神而異之。

translations.literal: And foolish men and foolish women, pretending [knowledge of] calendrical days and ghosts and spirits, wishing profit through fraud and deceit, cross-check against what they have seen and heard, use this to probe trivial near-at-hand matters, and treat it as miraculous and wondrous.
translations.idiomatic: Foolish men and foolish women, pretending knowledge of calendrical days and ghosts and spirits, seek profit through fraud, cross-check against what they have seen and heard, use this to probe trivial everyday matters, and treat it as miraculous and wondrous.

sentences.zh: 近者，風俗近巫，此誠弊俗。

translations.literal: Recently custom has drawn near to shamanism—this is truly a corrupt custom.
translations.idiomatic: Lately custom has drawn close to shamanism—this is truly a corrupt practice.

sentences.zh: 聖旨所及，實辨邪源。

translations.literal: What the sacred command touches truly distinguishes the source of perversity.
translations.idiomatic: What Your Majesty's inquiry touches truly distinguishes the source of perversity.

sentences.zh: 但存而不論，弊斯息矣。」

translations.literal: If one preserves [this insight] without discussing it further, the corruption will cease."
translations.idiomatic: If one keeps this insight in mind without dwelling on it further, the corruption will cease.

translations.literal: Close of reply.
translations.idiomatic: Close of reply.

sentences.zh: 他日延英，上曰：「朕讀《玄宗實錄》，見開元致理，天寶兆亂。

translations.literal: Another day at Yanying Hall, the emperor said: "I read the Veritable Records of Emperor Xuanzong and saw that the Kaiyuan era achieved good order while the Tianbao era foreshadowed disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Another day at Yanying Hall, the emperor said, "I read the Veritable Records of Emperor Xuanzong and saw that the Kaiyuan era achieved good order while the Tianbao era foreshadowed disorder.

sentences.zh: 事出一朝，治亂相反，何也？」

translations.literal: Events issued from a single reign—order and disorder opposed each other—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Both came from a single reign, yet order and disorder were opposites—why?"

sentences.zh: 絳對曰：

translations.literal: Jiang replied:
translations.idiomatic: Jiang replied:

sentences.zh: 臣聞理生於危心，亂生於肆誌。

translations.literal: I have heard that good order arises from a wary heart, and disorder arises from an unrestrained will.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that good order arises from a wary heart, and disorder arises from an unrestrained will.

sentences.zh: 玄宗自天後朝出居籓邸，嘗蒞官守，接時賢於外，知人事之艱難。

translations.literal: Since the reign of Empress Wu, Xuanzong went out to reside at his princely residence, once held official posts and local commands, met men of talent outside [the palace], and knew the hardships of human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From the reign of Empress Wu onward, Xuanzong lived outside the palace at his princely residence, once held local office, met men of talent in the world beyond, and knew the hardships of human affairs.

sentences.zh: 臨禦之初，任姚崇、宋璟，二人皆忠鯁上才，動以致主為心。

translations.literal: At the beginning of his accession he employed Yao Chong and Song Jing—both were loyal and outstanding talents who took benefiting the sovereign as their constant aim.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of his reign he employed Yao Chong and Song Jing—both were loyal and outstanding talents who took serving the sovereign well as their constant aim.

sentences.zh: 明皇乘思理之初，亦勵精聽納，故當時名賢在位，左右前後，皆尚忠正。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming also, riding the beginning of his resolve for good order, likewise exerted his spirit and listened and accepted [counsel]; therefore eminent worthies of the time held office all around him, and those to left and right and before and behind all prized loyalty and rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming, seizing the beginning of his resolve for good order, likewise exerted himself and listened and accepted counsel; therefore eminent worthies of the time held office all around him, and those at his side all prized loyalty and rectitude.

sentences.zh: 是以君臣交泰，內外寧謐。

translations.literal: Thus ruler and ministers enjoyed mutual harmony, and within and without were tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ruler and ministers enjoyed mutual harmony, and within and without the court were tranquil.

sentences.zh: 開元二十年以後，李林甫、楊國忠相繼用事，專引柔佞之人，分居要劇，茍媚於上，不聞直言。

translations.literal: After the twentieth year of Kaiyuan, Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong successively held power, exclusively bringing in soft and fawning men to fill key and urgent posts, fawning on the sovereign without hearing straight speech.
translations.idiomatic: After the twentieth year of Kaiyuan, Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong successively held power, bringing in only soft and fawning men to fill key posts, flattering the sovereign while straight speech went unheard.

sentences.zh: 嗜欲轉熾，國用不足，奸臣說以興利，武夫說以開邊。

translations.literal: Appetites and desires grew ever fiercer; state revenues were insufficient; villainous ministers urged profit-making measures, and military men urged opening the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Appetites and desires grew ever fiercer; state revenues were insufficient; villainous ministers urged profit-making schemes, and military men urged opening the frontier.

sentences.zh: 天下騷動，奸盜乘隙，遂至兩都覆敗，四海沸騰，乘輿播遷，幾至難復。

translations.literal: The realm was thrown into turmoil; villains and bandits seized the gap; it reached the point where both capitals were overthrown, the four seas boiled with unrest, the imperial carriage was driven to wander, and restoration was nearly impossible.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was thrown into turmoil; villains and bandits seized the opportunity; both capitals were overthrown, the four seas boiled with unrest, the imperial carriage was driven into exile, and restoration was nearly impossible.

sentences.zh: 蓋小人啟導，縱逸生驕之致也。

translations.literal: This was the outcome of petty men opening the way and indulgence giving birth to arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: This was the outcome of petty men opening the way and indulgence breeding arrogance.

sentences.zh: 至今兵宿兩河，西疆削盡，甿戶雕耗，府藏空虛，皆因天寶喪亂，以至於此。

translations.literal: To this day troops are quartered in the two He [provinces], the western borders have been wholly cut away, farming households are wasted and depleted, and treasury stores are empty—all because of the Tianbao calamity and disorder, leading to this.
translations.idiomatic: To this day troops remain quartered in the two He provinces, the western borders have been wholly lost, farming households are wasted and depleted, and the treasuries are empty—all because of the Tianbao calamity and disorder.

sentences.zh: 安危理亂，實系時主所行。

translations.literal: Security and danger, order and disorder, truly depend on what the ruler of the age does.
translations.idiomatic: Security and danger, order and disorder, truly depend on what the ruler of the age does.

sentences.zh: 陛下思廣天聰，親覽國史，垂意精賾，鑒於化源，實天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Your Majesty thinks to broaden Heaven's hearing, personally peruses the national histories, extends attention to subtle depths, and takes the source of transformation as mirror—truly the world's great fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty seeks to broaden Heaven's hearing, personally reads the national histories, extends attention to subtle depths, and takes the source of transformation as a mirror—truly the world's great fortune.

sentences.zh: 上又曰：「凡人行事，常患不通於理，已然之失，追悔誠難。

translations.literal: The emperor also said: "When any person acts, he often worries that he does not grasp principle; once a fault is done, it is truly hard to regret and amend it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also said, "When anyone acts, he often fears he does not grasp principle; once a fault is done, it is truly hard to regret and amend.

sentences.zh: 古人處此，復有道否？」

translations.literal: Did the ancients in this situation have a way [forward]?"
translations.idiomatic: Did the ancients in this situation have a way forward?"

sentences.zh: 絳對曰：「行事過差，聖哲皆所不免，故天子致諍臣以匡其失。

translations.literal: Jiang replied: "In acting with excessive error, even sages and wise men cannot avoid it; therefore the Son of Heaven brings forth remonstrating ministers to correct his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang replied, "Even sages and wise men cannot avoid acting with excessive error; therefore the Son of Heaven brings forth remonstrating ministers to correct his faults.

sentences.zh: 故主心理於中，臣論正於外，制理於未亂，銷患於未萌。

translations.literal: Thus the sovereign rectifies his mind within, ministers argue for correctness without, control order before disorder arises, and dissolve harm before it sprouts.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the sovereign rectifies his mind within, ministers argue for correctness without, establish order before disorder arises, and dissolve harm before it sprouts.

sentences.zh: 主或過舉，則諫以正之，故上下同體，猶手足之於心膂，交相為用，以致康寧。

translations.literal: If the sovereign oversteps, they remonstrate to correct him; thus upper and lower are one body, like hands and feet to the heart and spine, each acting for the other to achieve peace and well-being.
translations.idiomatic: If the sovereign oversteps, they remonstrate to correct him; thus ruler and ministers are one body, like hands and feet to the heart and spine, each serving the other to achieve peace and well-being.

sentences.zh: 此亦常理，非難遵之事。

translations.literal: This too is ordinary principle—not a hard thing to follow.
translations.idiomatic: This too is ordinary principle—not a difficult thing to follow.

sentences.zh: 但矜得護失，常情所蔽。

translations.literal: Yet pride in what one got right and shielding one's faults—ordinary feeling is blinded by this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet pride in what one got right and shielding one's faults—ordinary feeling is blinded by this.

sentences.zh: 古人貴改過不吝，從善如流，良為此也。

translations.literal: The ancients prized changing one's faults without stinginess and following good as if flowing with water—precisely for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients prized changing one's faults without stinginess and following good as if flowing with water—precisely for this reason.

sentences.zh: 臣等備位，無所發明，但陛下不廢芻言，則端士賢臣，必當自效。」

translations.literal: We hold our posts without offering anything illuminating—but if Your Majesty does not discard common speech, then upright gentlemen and worthy ministers will surely devote themselves of their own accord."
translations.idiomatic: We hold our posts without offering anything illuminating—but if Your Majesty does not discard common speech, then upright gentlemen and worthy ministers will surely devote themselves of their own accord."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕擢用卿等，所冀直言。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I promoted and employed you all because I hoped for straight speech.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I promoted and employed you all because I hoped for straight speech.

sentences.zh: 各宜盡心無隱，以匡不逮。

translations.literal: Each of you should devote your hearts without concealment to correct my shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: Each of you should devote your hearts without concealment to correct my shortcomings.

sentences.zh: 無以護失為慮也！」

translations.literal: Do not take shielding faults as a concern!"
translations.idiomatic: Do not let concern for shielding faults hold you back!

translations.literal: Close of edict.
translations.idiomatic: Close of edict.

sentences.zh: 其秋，魏博節度使田季安死，其子懷諫幼弱，軍中立其大將田興，使主軍事，興卒以六州之地歸命。

translations.literal: That autumn, Tian Ji'an, military governor of Weibo, died; his son Huaijian was young and weak; the army installed his great general Tian Xing to manage military affairs, and Xing ultimately submitted the six prefectures to imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, Tian Ji'an, military governor of Weibo, died; his son Huaijian was young and weak; the army installed his great general Tian Xing to manage military affairs, and Xing ultimately submitted the six prefectures to imperial authority.

sentences.zh: 其經始營創，皆絳之謀也。

translations.literal: The planning from the first founding was all Jiang's stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: The planning from the very beginning was all Jiang's doing.

sentences.zh: 時教坊忽稱密旨，取良家士女及衣冠別第妓人，京師囂然。

translations.literal: At the time the Music Bureau suddenly claimed a secret order and took daughters of good families and courtesans from the separate mansions of officials and gentry; the capital was in an uproar.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Music Bureau suddenly claimed a secret order and took daughters of good families and courtesans from the separate mansions of officials and gentry; the capital was in an uproar.

sentences.zh: 絳謂同列曰：「此事大虧損聖德，須有論諫。」

translations.literal: Jiang said to his colleagues: "This affair greatly injures sage virtue; there must be remonstrance on it."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang said to his colleagues, "This affair greatly injures Your Majesty's virtue; there must be remonstrance on it."

sentences.zh: 或曰：「此嗜欲間事，自有諫官論列。」

translations.literal: Someone said: "This is a matter among appetites and desires; remonstrating officials will discuss it on their own."
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "This is a matter of appetite and desire; remonstrating officials will discuss it on their own."

sentences.zh: 絳曰：「相公居常病諫官論事，此難事即推與諫官，可乎？」

translations.literal: Jiang said: "You chancellors usually complain when remonstrating officials discuss affairs—for a difficult matter to shove it off on remonstrating officials, is that acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiang said, "You chancellors usually complain when remonstrating officials discuss affairs—for a difficult matter to shove it off on remonstrating officials, is that acceptable?"

sentences.zh: 乃極言論奏。

translations.literal: [He] then presented a memorial arguing the point to the full.
translations.idiomatic: He then presented a memorial arguing the point to the full.

sentences.zh: 翌日延英，憲宗舉手謂絳曰：「昨見卿狀所論采擇事，非卿盡忠於朕，何以及此？

translations.literal: The next day at Yanying Hall, Xianzong raised his hand and said to Jiang: "Yesterday I saw your memorial discussing the selection affair—if you had not been fully loyal to me, how could it have reached this?
translations.idiomatic: The next day at Yanying Hall, Xianzong raised his hand and said to Jiang, "Yesterday I saw your memorial on the selection affair—if you had not been fully loyal to me, how could I have learned of this?

sentences.zh: 朕都不知向外事，此是教坊罪過，不諭朕意，以至於此。

translations.literal: I knew nothing at all of outside affairs; this is the Music Bureau's fault—they did not explain my intent, leading to this.
translations.idiomatic: I knew nothing at all of outside affairs; this is the Music Bureau's fault—they did not explain my intent and so things reached this point.

sentences.zh: 朕緣丹王已下四人，院中都無侍者，朕令於樂工中及閭裏有情願者，厚其錢帛，只取四人，四王各與一人。

translations.literal: Because from Prince Dan downward the four princes had no attendants in their residences, I ordered that among musicians and in the lanes those willing should be paid generously—we would take only four, one for each of the four princes.
translations.idiomatic: Because from Prince Dan downward the four princes had no attendants in their residences, I ordered that among musicians and in the lanes those willing should be paid generously—we would take only four, one for each of the four princes.

sentences.zh: 伊不會朕意，便如此生事。

translations.literal: They did not grasp my intent and went and made trouble like this.
translations.idiomatic: They did not grasp my intent and went and made trouble like this.

sentences.zh: 朕已令科罰，其所取人，並已放歸。

translations.literal: I have already ordered punishments assessed; those who were taken have all been sent home.
translations.idiomatic: I have already ordered punishments assessed; those who were taken have all been sent home.

sentences.zh: 若非卿言，朕寧知此過？」

translations.literal: If not for your words, how would I have known of this fault?"
translations.idiomatic: If not for your words, how would I have known of this fault?

translations.literal: Close of reply.
translations.idiomatic: Close of reply.

sentences.zh: 八年，封高邑縣男。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoyi County.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoyi County.

sentences.zh: 絳以足疾，拜章求免。

translations.literal: Jiang, because of a foot ailment, submitted a memorial requesting dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang, because of a foot ailment, submitted a memorial requesting dismissal.

sentences.zh: 九年，罷知政事，授禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was removed from managing state affairs and appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was removed from managing state affairs and appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十年，檢校戶部尚書，出為華州刺史。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was made honorary Minister of Revenue and sent out as governor of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was made honorary Minister of Revenue and sent out as governor of Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未幾，入為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he returned as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he returned as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 十四年，檢校吏部尚書，出為河中觀察使。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was made honorary Minister of the Civil Service and sent out as Intendant of Hedong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was made honorary Minister of the Civil Service and sent out as Intendant of Hedong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 河中舊為節制，皇甫镈惡絳，只以觀察命之。

translations.literal: Hedong had formerly been a military command; Huangfu Bo hated Jiang and appointed him only as intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong had formerly been a military command; Huangfu Bo hated Jiang and appointed him only as intendant.

sentences.zh: 十五年，镈得罪，絳復為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Bo fell from grace, and Jiang was again made Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Bo fell from grace, and Jiang was again made Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，改御史大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong ascended the throne, Jiang was reassigned as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong ascended the throne, Jiang was reassigned as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 穆宗亟於畋遊行幸，絳於延英切諫，帝不能用。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong was eager for hunting tours and imperial progresses; Jiang remonstrated urgently in Yanying Hall, but the emperor would not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong was eager for hunting tours and imperial progresses; Jiang remonstrated urgently in Yanying Hall, but the emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 絳以疾辭，復為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Jiang resigned on grounds of illness and was again made Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang resigned on grounds of illness and was again made Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年，轉吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changqing he was transferred to Minister of the Civil Service.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Changqing he was transferred to Minister of the Civil Service.

sentences.zh: 是歲，加檢校尚書右僕射，判東都尚書省事，充東都留守。

translations.literal: That year he was additionally made Honorary Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, oversaw the Eastern Capital office of the Department of State Affairs, and served as Defender of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was additionally made Honorary Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, oversaw the Eastern Capital office of the Department of State Affairs, and served as Defender of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，檢校本官、兗州刺史、兗海節度觀察待使。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year he was made honorary to his existing rank, Governor of Yan Prefecture, and military governor and intendant of Yan-Hai Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year he was made honorary to his existing rank, Governor of Yan Prefecture, and military governor and intendant of Yan-Hai Circuit.

sentences.zh: 三年，復為東都留守。

translations.literal: In the third year he again served as Defender of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he again served as Defender of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 四年，就加檢校司空。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was immediately additionally made Honorary Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was immediately additionally made Honorary Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 寶歷初，入為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Baoli reign he entered court as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Baoli reign he entered court as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二年九月，昭議節度使劉悟卒，遺表請以子從諫嗣襲，將吏詣闕論請。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year, Liu Wu, military governor of Zhaoyi Circuit, died; his final memorial asked that his son Congjian succeed and inherit the post, and the generals and officials went to the palace gate to petition for this.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year, Liu Wu, military governor of Zhaoyi Circuit, died; his final memorial asked that his son Congjian succeed and inherit the post, and the generals and officials went to the palace gate to petition for this.

sentences.zh: 絳密奏請速除近澤潞四面將帥一人，以充節度；

translations.literal: Jiang secretly memorialized asking that one general from the four sides near Ze and Lu be quickly appointed to fill the military governorship;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang secretly memorialized asking that one general from the four sides near Ze and Lu be quickly appointed to fill the military governorship;

sentences.zh: 令倍程赴鎮，使從諫未及拒命，新使已到，所謂「疾雷不及掩耳」。

translations.literal: he should be ordered to reach the command post at double speed, so that before Congjian could refuse the order the new envoy would already have arrived—what is called 'swift thunder gives no time to cover one's ears.'
translations.idiomatic: he should be ordered to reach the command post at double speed, so that before Congjian could refuse the order the new envoy would already have arrived—what is called 'swift thunder gives no time to cover one's ears.'

sentences.zh: 潞州軍心，自有所系。

translations.literal: The hearts of the Lu Prefecture army would naturally attach themselves elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: The hearts of the Lu Prefecture army would naturally attach themselves elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 從諫無位，何名主張。

translations.literal: Congjian would have no position—by what name could he assert authority?
translations.idiomatic: Congjian would have no position—by what name could he assert authority?

sentences.zh: 時宰相李逢吉、王守澄已受從諫賂，俱請以從諫留後，不能用絳言。

translations.literal: At the time the chief ministers Li Fengji and Wang Shoucheng had already received bribes from Congjian; both asked that Congjian be made regent-in-waiting, and Jiang's advice was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the chief ministers Li Fengji and Wang Shoucheng had already accepted bribes from Congjian; both asked that Congjian be made regent-in-waiting, and Jiang's advice was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 絳以直道進退，聞望傾於一時。

translations.literal: Jiang advanced and withdrew by the straight path, and his renown tilted the age for a time.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang advanced and withdrew by upright conduct, and for a time his renown eclipsed all others.

sentences.zh: 然剛腸嫉惡，賢不肖太分，以此為非正之徒所忌。

translations.literal: Yet his stiff spirit hated evil, and he divided the worthy and unworthy too sharply; for this he was resented by men of improper conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was stiff-spirited and hated evil, and he divided the worthy from the unworthy too sharply; for this he was resented by men of improper conduct.

sentences.zh: 又嘗與御史中丞王播相遇於道，播不為之避；

translations.literal: He also once met Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Bo on the road, and Bo did not yield to him;
translations.idiomatic: He also once met Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Bo on the road, and Bo did not yield to him;

sentences.zh: 絳奏論事體，敕命兩省詳議，鹹以絳論奏是。

translations.literal: Jiang memorialized discussing the propriety of the matter; an edict ordered the two departments to deliberate in detail, and all agreed that Jiang's memorial was correct.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang memorialized discussing the propriety of the matter; an edict ordered the two departments to deliberate in detail, and all agreed that Jiang's memorial was correct.

sentences.zh: 李逢吉佑播惡絳，乃罷絳僕射，改授太子少師，分司東都。

translations.literal: Li Fengji shielded Bo and harmed Jiang, then removed Jiang from the vice directorship and reassigned him as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, serving in the Eastern Capital in a nominal capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fengji shielded Bo and harmed Jiang, then removed Jiang from the vice directorship and reassigned him as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, serving in the Eastern Capital in a nominal capacity.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，征為太常卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, Jiang was summoned as Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, Jiang was summoned as Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 二年，檢校司空，出為興元尹、山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year he was made Honorary Minister of Works and sent out as Governor of Xingyuan and military governor of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made Honorary Minister of Works and sent out as Governor of Xingyuan and military governor of Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，南蠻寇西蜀，詔征赴援。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year, southern barbarians raided western Shu, and an edict ordered Jiang to go to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year, southern barbarians raided western Shu, and an edict ordered Jiang to go to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 絳於本道募兵千人赴蜀；

translations.literal: Jiang raised a thousand troops in his circuit to go to Shu;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang raised a thousand troops in his circuit to go to Shu;

sentences.zh: 及中路，蠻軍已退，所募皆還。

translations.literal: By the time they were halfway, the barbarian army had already withdrawn, and all those recruited returned.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they were halfway, the barbarian army had already withdrawn, and all those recruited returned.

sentences.zh: 興元兵額素定，募卒悉令罷歸。

translations.literal: The troop quota for Xingyuan had long been fixed, and all the recruited soldiers were ordered dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: The troop quota for Xingyuan had long been fixed, and all the recruited soldiers were ordered dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 四年二月十日，絳晨興視事，召募卒，以詔旨喻而遣之，仍給以廩麥，皆怏怏而退。

translations.literal: On the tenth day of the second month of the fourth year, Jiang rose early to attend to business, summoned the recruited soldiers, explained the edict and dismissed them, and still gave them grain rations—but all withdrew resentfully.
translations.idiomatic: On the tenth day of the second month of the fourth year, Jiang rose early to attend to business, summoned the recruited soldiers, explained the edict and dismissed them, and still gave them grain rations—but all withdrew resentfully.

sentences.zh: 監軍使楊叔元貪財怙寵，怨絳不奉己，乃因募卒賞薄，眾辭之際，以言激之，欲其為亂，以逞私憾。

translations.literal: The army supervisor Yang Shuyuan was greedy for wealth and relied on favor; resentful that Jiang did not defer to him, he took advantage of the moment when the recruited soldiers were complaining that their rewards were meager and incited them with words, wanting them to make trouble so he could satisfy a private grudge.
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisor Yang Shuyuan was greedy for wealth and relied on imperial favor; resentful that Jiang did not defer to him, he took advantage of the moment when the recruited soldiers were complaining that their rewards were meager and incited them with words, wanting them to make trouble so he could satisfy a private grudge.

sentences.zh: 募卒因監軍之言，怒氣益甚，乃噪聚趨府，劫庫兵以入使衙。

translations.literal: Because of the supervisor's words, the recruited soldiers' anger grew still fiercer; they then clamored together and rushed to the headquarters, seized weapons from the armory, and entered the commissioner's yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the supervisor's words, the recruited soldiers' anger grew still fiercer; they then clamored together and rushed to the headquarters, seized weapons from the armory, and entered the commissioner's yamen.

sentences.zh: 絳方與賓僚會宴，不及設備。

translations.literal: Jiang was just feasting with guests and retainers and had no time to prepare defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang was just feasting with guests and retainers and had no time to prepare defenses.

sentences.zh: 聞亂北走登陴，衙將王景延力戰以禦之。

translations.literal: Hearing the disturbance he fled north and climbed the ramparts; yamen guard Wang Jingyan fought hard to repel them.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the disturbance he fled north and climbed the ramparts; yamen guard Wang Jingyan fought hard to repel them.

sentences.zh: 兵折矢窮，景延死。

translations.literal: When their arrows were spent and broken, Jingyan died.
translations.idiomatic: When their arrows were spent and broken, Jingyan died.

sentences.zh: 絳乃為亂兵所害，時年六十七。

translations.literal: Jiang was then killed by the mutinous soldiers; he was sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang was then killed by the mutinous soldiers; he was sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 絳初登陴，左右請絳縋城，可以避免，絳不從。

translations.literal: When Jiang first climbed the ramparts, those beside him asked Jiang to let himself down from the city by rope, saying he could avoid harm; Jiang would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang first climbed the ramparts, those beside him asked Jiang to let himself down from the city by rope, saying he could avoid harm; Jiang would not agree.

sentences.zh: 乃並從事趙存約、薛齊俱死焉。

translations.literal: Then together with staff members Zhao Cunyue and Xue Qi he died as well.
translations.idiomatic: Then together with staff members Zhao Cunyue and Xue Qi he died as well.

sentences.zh: 文宗聞奏震悼，下制曰：「朝有正人，時稱令德，入參廟算，出總師幹。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong received the report he was shocked and grieved, and issued an edict saying: "When the court has an upright man, the age calls his virtue admirable; within he assists in the plans of the ancestral temple, without he commands the staffs of armies.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong received the report he was shocked and grieved, and issued an edict saying: "When the court has an upright man, the age calls his virtue admirable; within he assists in the plans of the ancestral temple, without he commands the staffs of armies.

sentences.zh: 方當寵任之臣，橫罹不幸之酷。

translations.literal: Just as he was a minister being showered with favor, he suffered the cruel blow of sudden misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was a minister being showered with favor, he suffered the cruel blow of sudden misfortune.

sentences.zh: 殄瘁興嘆，搢紳所同。

translations.literal: The withering away evokes sighs; officials and gentry share the grief.
translations.idiomatic: The devastation evokes sighs; officials and gentry share the grief.

sentences.zh: 故山南西道節度、管內觀察處置等使、銀青光祿大夫、檢校司空，兼興元尹、御史大夫、上柱國、趙郡開國公、食邑二千戶李絳，神授聰明，天賦清直。

translations.literal: The former Military Governor of Shannan West Circuit, Disposition Commissioner for the Circuit and Adjacent Areas, Silver-Glitter Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Honorary Minister of Works, Concurrent Governor of Xingyuan Prefecture, Censor-in-Chief, Supreme Pillar of the State, Duke of Zhao Commandery with a fief of two thousand households, Li Jiang—spirit endowed him with intelligence, Heaven gifted him with clean uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: The former Military Governor of Shannan West Circuit, Disposition Commissioner for the Circuit and Adjacent Areas, Silver-Glitter Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Honorary Minister of Works, Concurrent Governor of Xingyuan Prefecture, Censor-in-Chief, Supreme Pillar of the State, Duke of Zhao Commandery with a fief of two thousand households, Li Jiang—spirit endowed him with intelligence, Heaven gifted him with clean uprightness.

sentences.zh: 抱仁義以希前哲，立標準以程後來。

translations.literal: He embraced benevolence and righteousness in emulation of earlier sages and set standards to measure those who came after.
translations.idiomatic: He embraced benevolence and righteousness in emulation of earlier sages and set standards to measure those who came after.

sentences.zh: 抑揚時情，坐致臺輔。

translations.literal: He checked and lifted the temper of the age and by sitting upright attained the highest offices.
translations.idiomatic: He moderated the temper of the age and, without striving, attained the highest offices.

sentences.zh: 佐我烈祖，格於皇天。

translations.literal: He assisted our august ancestor and was attested by August Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He assisted our august ancestor and was attested by August Heaven.

sentences.zh: 仗鉞宣風，聯居樂土。

translations.literal: Bearing the axe he spread authority; he dwelt in succession on favored soil.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing the battle-axe he spread imperial authority; he dwelt in succession on favored soil.

sentences.zh: 乘軒鳴玉，嘗極清班。

translations.literal: Riding in carriage with jade chimes sounding, he once reached the most exalted ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Riding in carriage with jade chimes sounding, he once reached the most exalted ranks.

sentences.zh: 先聲而物議皆歸，不約而群情自許。

translations.literal: His reputation went before him and public opinion all turned to him; without being summoned, the feelings of the multitude pledged themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation went before him and public opinion all turned his way; without being summoned, the multitude pledged themselves to him.

sentences.zh: 漢中名部，俾遂便安。

translations.literal: In the famed commandery of Hanzhong, he was enabled to settle in ease.
translations.idiomatic: In the famed commandery of Hanzhong, he was enabled to settle in ease.

sentences.zh: 而變起不圖，禍生無兆。

translations.literal: Yet change arose unplanned, and disaster was born without warning.
translations.idiomatic: Yet change arose unplanned, and disaster was born without warning.

sentences.zh: 殲良之慟，聞訃增傷。

translations.literal: The grief at the slaying of the good man deepens at the news of his death.
translations.idiomatic: The grief at the slaying of the good man deepens at the news of his death.

sentences.zh: 是極哀榮，用優典禮。

translations.literal: Therefore let the utmost mourning honor be shown, and let exceptional rites be used.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore let the utmost mourning honor be shown, and let exceptional rites be used.

sentences.zh: 三公正秩，品數甚崇，式表異恩，以攄沈痛。

translations.literal: The three high ranks of the Three Excellencies are very exalted in grade; let them express extraordinary grace and pour out deep grief.
translations.idiomatic: The three high ranks of the Three Excellencies are very exalted in grade; let them express extraordinary grace and pour out deep grief.

sentences.zh: 可贈司徒。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously appointed Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He may be posthumously appointed Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 仍令所司擇日備禮冊命。」

translations.literal: Let the responsible offices also choose a day and prepare the rites of investiture."
translations.idiomatic: Let the responsible offices also choose a day and prepare the rites of investiture."

sentences.zh: 賻布帛三千段、米粟二百碩。

translations.literal: Funeral gifts of three thousand bolts of silk and cloth and two hundred shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral gifts of three thousand bolts of silk and cloth and two hundred shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 子璋、頊。

translations.literal: His sons were Zhang and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Zhang and Xu.

sentences.zh: 璋，登進士第。

translations.literal: Zhang passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 盧鈞鎮太原，辟為從事。

translations.literal: When Lu Jun governed Taiyuan, he recruited Zhang as a staff member.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Jun governed Taiyuan, he recruited Zhang as a staff member.

sentences.zh: 大中末，入朝為監察，轉侍御史。

translations.literal: Late in the Dazhong reign he entered court as investigating censor and was transferred to attending censor.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Dazhong reign he entered court as investigating censor and was transferred to attending censor.

sentences.zh: 出刺兩郡，終宣歙觀察使。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of two prefectures and ended as Intendant of Xuan and She.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as prefect of two prefectures and ended as Intendant of Xuan and She.

sentences.zh: 子德林。

translations.literal: His son was Delin.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Delin.

sentences.zh: 楊於陵，字達夫，弘農人。

translations.literal: Yang Yuling, Yang Yuling, style name Dafu, a man of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuling, whose style name was Dafu, was a man of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 漢太尉震之第五子奉之後。

translations.literal: A descendant of Feng, fifth son of Zhen, Grand Commandant of Han.
translations.idiomatic: He was a descendant of Feng, fifth son of Zhen, Grand Commandant of Han.

sentences.zh: 曾祖珪，為辰州掾曹。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Gui was a staff officer in Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Gui was a staff officer in Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖冠俗，奉先尉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Guansu was magistrate of Fengxian.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Guansu was magistrate of Fengxian.

sentences.zh: 父太清，宋州單父尉。

translations.literal: His father Taiqing was magistrate of Shanfu in Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Taiqing was magistrate of Shanfu in Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 於陵，天寶末家寄河朔。

translations.literal: Yuling's family settled in Hebei late in the Tianbao reign.
translations.idiomatic: Yuling's family settled in Hebei late in the Tianbao reign.

sentences.zh: 祿山亂，其父歿於賊，於陵始六歲。

translations.literal: When the An Lushan rebellion broke out, his father died at the hands of the rebels; Yuling was then six.
translations.idiomatic: When the An Lushan rebellion broke out, his father died at the hands of the rebels; Yuling was then six.

sentences.zh: 及長，客於江南。

translations.literal: When he grew up he lived as a guest in the south.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he lived as a guest in the south.

sentences.zh: 好學，有奇誌。

translations.literal: He loved learning and had an unusual will.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and had an unusual will.

sentences.zh: 弱冠舉進士，釋褐為潤州句容主簿。

translations.literal: At twenty he passed the jinshi examination, doffed his commoner's garb, and was appointed chief clerk of Jurong in Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he passed the jinshi examination, doffed his commoner's garb, and was appointed chief clerk of Jurong in Run Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時韓滉節制金陵，滉性剛嚴，少所接與。

translations.literal: At the time Han Huang controlled Jinling; Huang's nature was stern and hard, and he received few people.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Han Huang controlled Jinling; Huang's nature was stern and hard, and he received few people.

sentences.zh: 及於陵以屬吏謁謝，滉甚奇之，謂其妻柳氏曰：「夫人常擇佳婿，吾閱人多矣，無如楊主簿者。」

translations.literal: When Yuling came to pay his respects as a subordinate official, Huang was greatly impressed and said to his wife Lady Liu: "Madam often chooses a fine son-in-law; I have reviewed many men, and none is like Chief Clerk Yang."
translations.idiomatic: When Yuling came to pay his respects as a subordinate official, Huang was greatly impressed and said to his wife Lady Liu: "Madam often chooses a fine son-in-law; I have reviewed many men, and none is like Chief Clerk Yang."

sentences.zh: 後竟以女妻之。

translations.literal: In the end he gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，為鄂嶽、江南二府從事，累官至侍御史。

translations.literal: When his term expired he served as staff member in the E-Yue and Jiangnan prefectural offices, and rose in successive posts to attending censor.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he served as staff member in the E-Yue and Jiangnan prefectural offices, and rose in successive posts to attending censor.

sentences.zh: 韓滉自江南入朝，總將相財賦之任，頗承顧遇，權傾中外。

translations.literal: When Han Huang entered court from Jiangnan he took charge of the finances of generals and ministers and received considerable favor; his power tilted inside and outside the court.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Huang entered court from Jiangnan he took charge of the finances of generals and ministers and received considerable favor; his power tilted inside and outside the court.

sentences.zh: 於陵自江西府罷，以婦翁權幸方熾，不欲進取。

translations.literal: Yuling left the Jiangxi prefectural office; because his father-in-law's power and favor were then blazing, he did not wish to seek advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Yuling left the Jiangxi prefectural office; because his father-in-law's power and favor were then blazing, he did not wish to seek advancement.

sentences.zh: 乃卜築於建昌，以讀書山水為樂。

translations.literal: He then chose a site and built at Jianchang, taking reading and mountains and rivers as his pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: He then chose a site and built at Jianchang, taking reading and mountains and rivers as his pleasure.

sentences.zh: 滉歿，貞元八年始入朝，為膳部員外郎，歷考功、吏部三員外，判南曹。

translations.literal: When Huang died, Yuling first entered court in the eighth year of Zhenyuan, was appointed vice director in the Ministry of Rites, served in succession as vice director in the Ministries of Personnel Review and of the Civil Service, and adjudicated the Southern Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang died, Yuling first entered court in the eighth year of Zhenyuan, was appointed vice director in the Ministry of Rites, served in succession as vice director in the Ministries of Personnel Review and of the Civil Service, and adjudicated the Southern Bureau.

sentences.zh: 時宰相有密親調集，文書不如式，於陵駁之，大協物論。

translations.literal: At the time a chief minister had a close relative under consideration for appointment, and the documents were not in proper form; Yuling rejected them, greatly matching public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a chief minister had a close relative under consideration for appointment, and the documents were not in proper form; Yuling rejected them, greatly matching public opinion.

sentences.zh: 遷右司郎中，復轉吏部郎中，改京兆少尹。

translations.literal: He was promoted to director in the Left Department, then transferred to director in the Ministry of the Civil Service, and was changed to Vice Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director in the Left Department, then transferred to director in the Ministry of the Civil Service, and was changed to Vice Governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 出為絳州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as governor of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as governor of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 德宗雅聞其名，將辭赴郡，詔留之，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong had long heard his name; when he was about to leave for his prefecture an edict kept him and he was appointed Drafting Secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong had long heard his name; when he was about to leave for his prefecture an edict kept him and he was appointed Drafting Secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時李實為京兆尹，恃承恩寵，於陵與給事中許孟容俱不附協，為實媒孽，孟容改太常少卿，於陵為秘書少監。

translations.literal: At the time Li Shi was metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, relying on imperial favor; Yuling and Supervising Secretary Xu Mengrong both refused to go along, and Shi slandered them—Mengrong was changed to Vice Minister of Ceremonies, and Yuling to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
