translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Shi was metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, relying on imperial favor; Yuling and Supervising Secretary Xu Mengrong both refused to go along, and Shi slandered them—Mengrong was changed to Vice Minister of Ceremonies, and Yuling to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，實輩敗，遷於陵為華州刺史，充潼關防禦、鎮國軍等使。

translations.literal: Late in Zhenyuan, when Shi's faction fell, Yuling was moved to governor of Hua Prefecture and served as Defender of Tong Pass and commissioner of the Zhenguo Army and such posts.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Zhenyuan, when Shi's faction fell, Yuling was moved to governor of Hua Prefecture and served as Defender of Tong Pass and commissioner of the Zhenguo Army and such posts.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷浙江東道都團練觀察等使。

translations.literal: Before long he was moved to Unified Training and Intendant Commissioner of Zhejiang East Circuit and such posts.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was moved to Unified Training and Intendant Commissioner of Zhejiang East Circuit and such posts.

sentences.zh: 政聲流聞，入拜戶部侍郎，復改京兆尹。

translations.literal: His reputation for good administration spread; he entered court as Vice Minister of Revenue and was again changed to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation for good administration spread; he entered court as Vice Minister of Revenue and was again changed to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 先是，禁軍影占編戶，無以區別。

translations.literal: Previously, forbidden-army soldiers had shadow-enrolled in registered households, and there was no way to distinguish them.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, forbidden-army soldiers had shadow-enrolled in registered households, and there was no way to distinguish them.

sentences.zh: 自於陵請致挾名，每五丁者，得兩丁入軍，四丁、三丁者，各以條限。

translations.literal: From Yuling's request to expose false enrollments, for every five men two were taken into the army; for four or three men, each case followed the statutory limit.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuling's request the court exposed false enrollments: for every five men, two were drafted into the army; for groups of four or three, each case followed the statutory quota.

sentences.zh: 由是京師豪強，復知所畏。

translations.literal: Because of this the powerful clans of the capital again knew what to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this the powerful clans of the capital again knew what to fear.

sentences.zh: 再遷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 元和初，以考策，升直言極諫牛僧孺等，為執政所怒，出為嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe, because of the examination policy essays he advanced the blunt remonstrators Niu Sengru and others, and the chief ministers were angered and sent him out as military governor of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanhe, in grading the policy essays he passed the blunt remonstrators Niu Sengru and others; the chief ministers were angered and sent him out as military governor of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 會監軍使許遂振悍戾貪恣，幹撓軍政。

translations.literal: It happened that the army supervisor Xu Suizhen was fierce, greedy, and willful, and interfered in military administration.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the army supervisor Xu Suizhen was fierce, greedy, and willful, and interfered in military administration.

sentences.zh: 於陵奉公潔己，遂振無能奈何，乃以飛語上聞。

translations.literal: Yuling served the public and kept himself clean; Suizhen could do nothing about it, and so sent slanderous reports to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yuling served the public and kept himself clean; Suizhen could do nothing about it, and so sent slanderous reports to the throne.

sentences.zh: 憲宗驚惑，賴宰相裴垍為於陵申理，憲宗感悟。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong was alarmed and perplexed; relying on Chief Minister Pei Ji to plead Yuling's case, the emperor came to his senses.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong was alarmed and perplexed; relying on Chief Minister Pei Ji to plead Yuling's case, the emperor came to his senses.

sentences.zh: 五年，入為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he entered court as Vice Minister of the Civil Service.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he entered court as Vice Minister of the Civil Service.

sentences.zh: 遂振終自得罪。

translations.literal: Suizhen in the end brought guilt upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: Suizhen in the end brought guilt upon himself.

sentences.zh: 於陵為吏部，凡四周歲，監察奸吏，調補平允，當時稱之。

translations.literal: As Vice Minister of the Civil Service, Yuling served four full years, inspected corrupt officials, and made transfers and appointments fairly; the age praised him.
translations.idiomatic: As Vice Minister of the Civil Service, Yuling served four full years, inspected corrupt officials, and made transfers and appointments fairly; the age praised him.

sentences.zh: 初，吏部試判，別差考判官三人校能否，元和初罷之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Ministry of the Civil Service tested policy judgments, three specially assigned examination judges were sent separately to assess competence; at the beginning of Yuanhe this was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Ministry of the Civil Service tested policy judgments, three specially assigned examination judges were sent separately to assess competence; at the beginning of Yuanhe this was abolished.

sentences.zh: 七年，吏部尚書鄭余慶以疾請告，乃復置考判官，以兵部員外郎韋顗、屯田員外張仲素、太學博士陸亙等為之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when Minister of the Civil Service Zheng Yuqing requested leave on grounds of illness, the examination judges were again established, with Vice Director of War Wei Yi, Vice Director of Public Works Zhang Zhongsu, and Erudite of the Imperial Academy Lu Gen appointed to the posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when Minister of the Civil Service Zheng Yuqing requested leave on grounds of illness, the examination judges were again established, with Vice Director of War Wei Yi, Vice Director of Public Works Zhang Zhongsu, and Erudite of the Imperial Academy Lu Gen appointed to the posts.

sentences.zh: 於陵自東都來，言曰：「本司考判，自當公心。

translations.literal: Yuling came from the Eastern Capital and said: "Examination judgments in this ministry should naturally proceed from an impartial heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yuling came from the Eastern Capital and said, "Judging examinations in this ministry should naturally proceed from an impartial heart.

sentences.zh: 非次置官，不知曹內公事。

translations.literal: To appoint officials out of turn—they do not know the business inside the bureau.
translations.idiomatic: To appoint officials out of turn is wrong—they do not know the bureau's routine business.

sentences.zh: 考官只論判之能否，不計闕員；

translations.literal: The examiners consider only whether the case judgments are adequate, not whether posts are vacant;
translations.idiomatic: Examiners considered only whether case judgments were adequate, not whether posts stood vacant;

sentences.zh: 本司只計員闕幾何，定其留放。

translations.literal: the home office considers only how many vacancies exist and determines who is retained or released.
translations.idiomatic: the home office counted only how many vacancies existed and decided who would be kept or dismissed.

sentences.zh: 置官不便。」

translations.literal: Establishing offices is inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: Creating such offices was ill-advised.

sentences.zh: 宰執以已置顗等，只令考科目選人，其余常調，委本司自考。

translations.literal: The chief ministers, having already appointed Yan and others, ordered only examination-subject candidates to be tested; the rest of the regular transfers were entrusted to the home office for self-examination.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers, having already appointed Yan and others, ordered that only examination-subject candidates be tested; the remaining regular transfers were left to the home office to examine on its own.

sentences.zh: 於陵又以甲歷年深朽斷，吏緣為奸，奏換大歷七年至貞元二十年甲庫歷，令本司郎官監換。

translations.literal: Yuling also, because the appointment registers were old and rotten with breakage and clerks used this for fraud, memorialized to replace the register vault records from the seventh year of Dali through the twentieth year of Zhenyuan, ordering ministry directors to supervise the replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Yuling also found that the appointment registers had grown old and broken apart, giving clerks opportunity for fraud; he memorialized to replace the vault registers from the seventh year of Dali through the twentieth year of Zhenyuan and had ministry directors supervise the exchange.

sentences.zh: 九年，妖人楊叔高自廣州來幹於陵，請為己輔，於陵執奏殺之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the sorcerer Yang Shugao came from Guangzhou to seek Yuling's favor and asked to serve as his aide; Yuling had him arrested, memorialized, and executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the sorcerer Yang Shugao came from Guangzhou to approach Yuling and asked to serve as his aide; Yuling had him arrested, memorialized the throne, and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 改兵部侍郎、判度支。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Minister of War in charge of the Bureau of Budgets.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as vice minister of war in charge of the Bureau of Budgets.

sentences.zh: 時淮西用兵，於陵用所親為唐鄧供軍使，節度使高霞寓以供軍有闕，移牒度支，於陵不為之易，其闕如舊。

translations.literal: At the time troops were deployed in Huaixi; Yuling appointed a close associate as army-supply commissioner for Tang and Deng; Military Commissioner Gao Xiayu, because army supplies were short, sent a dispatch to the Bureau of Budgets, but Yuling would not change this, and the shortage remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: While the campaign in Huaixi was underway, Yuling appointed a close associate army-supply commissioner for Tang and Deng. When Military Commissioner Gao Xiayu reported shortages in army supplies and sent a dispatch to the Bureau of Budgets, Yuling would not alter the arrangement, and the shortfall remained.

sentences.zh: 霞寓軍屢有摧敗，詔書督責之；

translations.literal: Xiayu's army suffered repeated defeats, and imperial edicts pressed and rebuked him;
translations.idiomatic: Xiayu's army suffered repeated defeats, and imperial edicts pressed and rebuked him;

sentences.zh: 乃奏以度支饋運不繼。

translations.literal: he then memorialized that the Bureau of Budgets had failed to sustain transport of provisions.
translations.idiomatic: he then memorialized that the Bureau of Budgets had failed to keep provisions moving.

sentences.zh: 憲宗怒，

translations.literal: Xianzong grew angry,
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong grew angry,

sentences.zh: 十一年，貶於陵為桂陽郡守，量移原王傅。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Yuling was demoted to Administrator of Guiyang Commandery and shortly transferred to Tutor of the Prince of Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Yuling was demoted to administrator of Guiyang Commandery and soon transferred to tutor of the Prince of Yuan.

sentences.zh: 復遷戶部侍郎，知吏部選事。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue in charge of Ministry of Personnel selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to vice minister of revenue and put in charge of Ministry of Personnel selection affairs.

sentences.zh: 會誅李師道，分其地為三鎮，朝廷思有所制置，以於陵兼御史大夫，充淄、青十二州宣慰使，還奏合旨。

translations.literal: When Li Shidao was executed and his territory divided into three commands, the court wished to arrange governance; Yuling was made concurrently Censor-in-Chief and Pacification Commissioner for the twelve prefectures of Zi and Qing; on his return his memorial accorded with the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shidao was executed and his territory divided into three commands, the court sought to arrange governance. Yuling was made concurrently censor-in-chief and pacification commissioner for the twelve prefectures of Zi and Qing; on his return his report accorded with the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，遷戶部尚書。

translations.literal: When Muzong ascended the throne, Yuling was promoted to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong ascended the throne, Yuling was promoted to minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，拜太常卿，充東都留守，年高，拜章辭位。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changqing he was appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Defender of the Eastern Capital; advanced in years, he memorialized to resign his post.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Changqing he was appointed director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and defender of the Eastern Capital; advanced in years, he memorialized to resign.

sentences.zh: 寶歷二年，授檢校右僕射、兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoli he was granted concurrently Vice Director of the Right and Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoli he was granted concurrently vice director of the right and junior tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 旋以左僕射致仕，詔給全俸，懇讓不受。

translations.literal: Shortly he retired as Vice Director of the Left; an edict granted full salary, but he earnestly declined and would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he retired as vice director of the left; an edict granted him full salary, but he earnestly declined and would not accept it.

sentences.zh: 於陵器度弘雅，進止有常。

translations.literal: Yuling's bearing was broad and refined, and his conduct in advancing and withdrawing was constant.
translations.idiomatic: Yuling's bearing was broad and refined, and his conduct was always measured and proper.

sentences.zh: 居朝三十余年，踐更中外，始終不失其正。

translations.literal: He served at court more than thirty years, holding posts inside and outside in turn, and from beginning to end never lost his rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: He served at court more than thirty years, holding posts at court and in the provinces in turn, and never lost his rectitude from beginning to end.

sentences.zh: 居官奉職，亦善操守，時人皆仰其風德。

translations.literal: In office he fulfilled his duties and was also skilled in personal integrity; people of the time all looked up to his moral influence.
translations.idiomatic: In office he fulfilled his duties and maintained his integrity well; people of the time all admired his moral stature.

sentences.zh: 太和四年十月卒，年七十八，冊贈司空，謚貞孝。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Taihe he died at age seventy-eight; by patent he was posthumously enfeoffed Minister of Works with posthumous title Zhenxiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Taihe he died at the age of seventy-eight; he was posthumously enfeoffed as minister of works with the posthumous title Zhenxiao.

sentences.zh: 子四人：景復、嗣復、紹復、師復。

translations.literal: He had four sons: Jingfu, Sifu, Shaofu, and Shifu.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Jingfu, Sifu, Shaofu, and Shifu.

sentences.zh: 嗣復自有傳。

translations.literal: Sifu has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 景復位終同州刺史。

translations.literal: Jingfu's final post was Governor of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jingfu's final post was governor of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 紹復進士擢第，弘辭登科，位終中書舍人。

translations.literal: Shaofu was selected in the jinshi examination and passed the Hongci examination; his final post was Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Shaofu passed the jinshi examination and the Hongci examination; his final post was drafting attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 師復位終大理卿。

translations.literal: Shifu's final post was Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Shifu's final post was director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 大中後，楊氏諸子登進士第者十人：嗣復子授、技、拭、捴；

translations.literal: After Dazhong, ten sons of the Yang clan passed the jinshi examination: Sifu's sons Shou, Ji, Shi, and Zong;
translations.idiomatic: After the Dazhong era, ten sons of the Yang clan passed the jinshi examination: Sifu's sons Shou, Ji, Shi, and Zong;

sentences.zh: 紹復子擢、拯、據、揆；

translations.literal: Shaofu's sons Zhuo, Zheng, Ju, and Kui;
translations.idiomatic: Shaofu's sons Zhuo, Zheng, Ju, and Kui;

sentences.zh: 師復子拙、振等。

translations.literal: and Shifu's sons Zhuo, Zhen, and others.
translations.idiomatic: and Shifu's sons Zhuo, Zhen, and others.

sentences.zh: 擢終給事中。

translations.literal: Zhuo's final post was Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo's final post was attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 拯司封員外郎。

translations.literal: Zheng was Junior Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng served as junior director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 據右補闕。

translations.literal: Ju was Repletion Official on the Right.
translations.idiomatic: Ju was repletion official on the right.

sentences.zh: 揆左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Kui was Remonstrance Official on the Left.
translations.idiomatic: Kui was remonstrance official on the left.

sentences.zh: 拙左庶子。

translations.literal: Zhuo was Junior Mentor on the Left.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo was junior mentor on the left.

sentences.zh: 振左拾遺。

translations.literal: Zhen was Reminder on the Left.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was reminder on the left.

sentences.zh: 【贊】史臣曰：王氏二英，播、起位崇將相，善始令終。

translations.literal: [Commentary] The historian says: Two outstanding men of the Wang clan—Bo and Qi—rose to the rank of chief ministers and generals and had good beginnings and fine endings.
translations.idiomatic: [Commentary] The historian says: Two outstanding men of the Wang clan—Bo and Qi—rose to the rank of chief ministers and generals and began well and ended well.

sentences.zh: 而炎薄祐短齡，美鐘於鐸，而能驤首矯翼，淩厲亨衢，仗鉞秉衡，扶持衰運。

translations.literal: Yan had thin fortune and a short life; beauty was concentrated in Duo, who could raise his head and spread his wings, soar through the broad highway, bear the battle-axe and hold the scales, and support a declining age.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had thin fortune and a short life; excellence was concentrated in Duo, who could raise his head and spread his wings, soar along the broad highway, bear the battle-axe and hold the scales, and support a declining dynasty.

sentences.zh: 天胡罰善，遇盜而殂，悲哉！

translations.literal: Why does Heaven punish the good? He met bandits and perished—how tragic!
translations.idiomatic: Why does Heaven punish the good? He met bandits and perished—how tragic!

sentences.zh: 李趙公頡頏禁林，訏謨相府，嘉言啟沃，不以身為。

translations.literal: Duke Li of Zhao matched the Hanlin in stature, counseled at the chief minister's hall, offered fine words of nurture, and did not make himself the issue.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Li of Zhao matched the Hanlin in stature, counseled in the chief minister's hall, offered fine words of nurture, and did not make himself the issue.

sentences.zh: 糜軀將壇，沒有余裕。

translations.literal: He wore out his body at the command post and died without surplus of years.
translations.idiomatic: He wore out his body at the command post and died without years to spare.

sentences.zh: 楊僕射避婦翁之當軸，疏驕尹之怙權，守道居貞，壽考終吉，行己始卒，人以為難。

translations.literal: Vice Director Yang avoided his father-in-law holding the axis of power, kept his distance from an arrogant metropolitan governor who relied on authority, upheld the Way and dwelt in rectitude, lived long and ended auspiciously, and from beginning to end in his conduct was consistent—people considered this difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yang avoided his father-in-law holding the reins of power, kept his distance from an arrogant metropolitan governor who relied on authority, upheld the Way and dwelt in rectitude, lived long and died in peace, and from beginning to end in his conduct was consistent—people considered this difficult to achieve.

sentences.zh: 美哉！

translations.literal: How admirable!
translations.idiomatic: How admirable!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：王氏儒宗，一門三相。

translations.literal: The commentary says: The Wang clan were Confucian exemplars; one family produced three chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: The Wang clan were Confucian exemplars; one family produced three chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 趙公排擯，言猶鯁亮。

translations.literal: Duke of Zhao was driven out, yet his words remained sharp and bright.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Zhao was driven out, yet his words remained sharp and bright.

sentences.zh: 幹將雖折，不改其剛。

translations.literal: Though the keen blade was broken, its hardness was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Though the keen blade was broken, its hardness was unchanged.

sentences.zh: 楊君之德，《韶》、《夏》洋洋。

translations.literal: Lord Yang's virtue was vast as the Shaos and the Xias.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Yang's virtue was vast as the music of Shao and Xia.
